## Body

Found during the Cerberus baseline run (docs/perf/baseline-cerberus-2026-08-11.md, Anomalies): each scenario summary records `commit` via `git rev-parse` at scenario start. A concurrent session committing to the checkout during the ~7-minute matrix made 6 of 8 scenarios self-report commits whose code was never in the tested binary (binary mtime pinned the real unit under test to f9b047d). The field should pin the binary's identity (e.g. hash the binary, or record rev-parse once at `perf_require_binary` time alongside the binary mtime), not re-read HEAD per scenario.

Evidence: baseline doc's Anomalies section; scratch artifacts from the 2026-08-11 run.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/perf/common.sh — shared helpers for the P1-PERF load/stress harness.
3	#
4	# Sourced by every s*-*.sh scenario and by run-all.sh. Nothing here measures
5	# anything on its own; it supplies the four things every scenario needs:
6	#
7	#   * a scenario workspace   — fresh data dir + a seeded git repo (demo.sh's
8	#                              recipe: .sergeant/workflows/<name>/<stage>/)
9	#   * a daemon under control — spawned with a chosen SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT, its pid
10	#                              read from the runtime descriptor (the documented
11	#                              client handshake), stopped and verified stopped
12	#   * /proc sampling         — VmRSS / VmHWM / threads / fd count / utime+stime
13	#                              into CSV, either one row on demand or a
14	#                              background sampler at a chosen interval
15	#   * measurement plumbing   — latency timing, percentiles, a summary block
16	#                              that is printed and written as JSON, and the
17	#                              hygiene sweep
18	#
19	# The harness drives the shipped release binary and its loopback HTTP API and
20	# adds no Rust (P1-PERF non-goal: "new Rust code beyond what a scenario
21	# strictly needs"). High-rate cells drive POST /v1/... with curl rather than
22	# one CLI process per call, because the CLI spawns a process per call and that
23	# is the client's cost, not the daemon's.
24	#
25	# Nothing under here writes into the repository tree: every scenario's data
26	# dirs, repos and raw output live under the <outdir> it is given.
27	
28	# --- resolution ------------------------------------------------------------
29	
30	PERF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
31	PERF_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$PERF_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
32	# The unit under test is the release build (P1-PERF: "the baseline describes
33	# what ships, not debug-profile DuckDB").
34	SGT_BIN="${SGT_BIN:-$PERF_REPO_ROOT/target/release/sgt}"
35	
36	PERF_CLK_TCK="$(getconf CLK_TCK 2>/dev/null || echo 100)"
37	
38	# Timing: CLOCK_REALTIME nanoseconds. `date +%s%N` costs a fork (~2 ms on this
39	# container) which is the same order as the thing being measured, so the
40	# fork-free bash-5 EPOCHREALTIME is preferred and `date` is the fallback. Same
41	# clock, same units.
42	perf_now_ns() {
43	  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
44	  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
45	    t=${t/,/.}
46	    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
47	    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
48	    printf '%s%s\n' "$sec" "${frac:0:9}"
49	  else
50	    date +%s%N
51	  fi
52	}
53	
54	# perf_mark VAR — assign "now" in ns to VAR without forking a subshell.
55	perf_mark() {
56	  local -n __perf_mark_out=$1
57	  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
58	  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
59	    t=${t/,/.}
60	    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
61	    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
62	    __perf_mark_out="${sec}${frac:0:9}"
63	  else
64	    __perf_mark_out="$(date +%s%N)"
65	  fi
66	}
67	
68	perf_die() { printf '\033[31mperf: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
69	perf_say() { printf '   %s\n' "$*"; }
70	perf_step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
71	perf_warn() { printf '\033[33m   ! %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; }
72	
73	perf_require_binary() {
74	  [ -x "$SGT_BIN" ] || perf_die "no release binary at $SGT_BIN (cargo build --release)"
75	  for tool in curl jq python3 git; do
76	    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || perf_die "missing required tool: $tool"
77	  done
78	  # The tested binary's identity, captured exactly once — a live rev-parse per
79	  # scenario tracks the checkout, not the binary: a commit landing mid-matrix
80	  # made 6 of 8 scenarios self-report code that was never in the binary
81	  # (issue #50). Exported so scenarios spawned by run-all.sh inherit the pin
82	  # instead of re-reading HEAD.
83	  if [ -z "${PERF_COMMIT:-}" ]; then
84	    PERF_COMMIT="$(git -C "$PERF_REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
85	    export PERF_COMMIT
86	  fi
87	}
88	
89	# --- scenario lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------
90	
91	# perf_init <outdir> <scenario-name>
92	#
93	# Creates the output dir, the scenario's scratch dir (data dirs and seed repos
94	# live there, never in the repo tree), opens the summary accumulator, and
95	# installs the teardown trap so an aborted scenario still stops its daemon.
96	perf_init() {
97	  PERF_OUT="$1"
98	  PERF_SCENARIO="$2"
99	  perf_require_binary
100	  mkdir -p "$PERF_OUT"
101	  PERF_OUT="$(cd "$PERF_OUT" && pwd)"
102	  PERF_SCRATCH="$PERF_OUT/scratch"
103	  mkdir -p "$PERF_SCRATCH"
104	  PERF_SUMMARY_TSV="$PERF_OUT/${PERF_SCENARIO}-summary.tsv"
105	  : > "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV"
106	  PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
107	  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=""
108	  PERF_FORCE_KILLED=0
109	  PERF_REPOS=()
110	  PERF_START_NS="$(perf_now_ns)"
111	  trap 'perf_teardown' EXIT
112	  perf_step "$PERF_SCENARIO — output $PERF_OUT"
113	  perf_kv scenario "$PERF_SCENARIO"
114	  perf_kv binary "$SGT_BIN"
115	  perf_kv commit "$PERF_COMMIT"
116	  perf_kv started_at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
117	}
118	
119	perf_teardown() {
120	  local rc=$?
121	  perf_sampler_stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
122	  if [ -n "${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" ] && kill -0 "$PERF_DAEMON_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
123	    perf_daemon_stop "$PERF_DAEMON_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
124	  fi
125	  return $rc
126	}
127	
128	# --- the summary block -----------------------------------------------------
129	
130	# perf_kv <key> <value> — one distilled measurement.
131	perf_kv() { printf '%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" >> "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV"; }
132	
133	# perf_summary — print the distilled block and write <scenario>-summary.json.
134	perf_summary() {
135	  python3 - "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV" "$PERF_OUT/${PERF_SCENARIO}-summary.json" "$PERF_SCENARIO" <<'PY'
136	import json, sys
137	tsv, out, name = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
138	rows = []
139	for line in open(tsv):
140	    line = line.rstrip("\n")
141	    if not line:
142	        continue
143	    key, _, value = line.partition("\t")
144	    rows.append((key, value))
145	doc = {}
146	for key, value in rows:
147	    try:
148	        doc[key] = int(value)
149	    except ValueError:
150	        try:
151	            doc[key] = float(value)
152	        except ValueError:
153	            doc[key] = value
154	json.dump(doc, open(out, "w"), indent=2, sort_keys=False)
155	width = max((len(k) for k, _ in rows), default=0)
156	print()
157	print(f"\033[1m-- {name} summary " + "-" * max(0, 58 - len(name)) + "\033[0m")
158	for key, value in rows:
159	    print(f"   {key.ljust(width)}  {value}")
160	print(f"   (json: {out})")
161	PY
162	}
163	
164	# --- seed repo (demo.sh's recipe) ------------------------------------------
165	
166	# perf_seed_repo <repo-dir> [stage-count]
167	#
168	# A throwaway git repository carrying a `.sergeant/workflows/software-change`
169	# workflow — the same layout scripts/demo.sh builds, which is what makes the
170	# submit path materialize a surface and run stages instead of parking the work
171	# in `pending`.
172	perf_seed_repo() {
173	  local repo="$1" stages="${2:-2}"
174	  mkdir -p "$repo"
175	  git init -q -b main "$repo"
176	  git -C "$repo" config user.email perf@example.invalid
177	  git -C "$repo" config user.name "sgt perf harness"
178	  git -C "$repo" config commit.gpgsign false
179	  printf 'def settle(payment):\n    return gateway.settle(payment)\n' > "$repo/payments.py"
180	  local wf="$repo/.sergeant/workflows/software-change"
181	  mkdir -p "$wf"
182	  local names=(10-implement 20-review 30-verify 40-land 50-followup)
183	  local ids=() i id
184	  for ((i = 0; i < stages; i++)); do
185	    if [ "$i" -lt "${#names[@]}" ]; then id="${names[$i]}"; else id="$(printf '%02d-stage%d' $(((i + 1) * 10)) $((i + 1)))"; fi
186	    ids+=("$id")
187	    mkdir -p "$wf/$id"
188	    printf 'Stage %s of the perf workflow.\n' "$id" > "$wf/$id/CONTEXT.md"
189	  done
190	  {
191	    printf '[workflow]\nname = "software-change"\nversion = "1"\nstages = ['
192	    local sep=""
193	    for id in "${ids[@]}"; do printf '%s"%s"' "$sep" "$id"; sep=", "; done
194	    printf ']\n'
195	  } > "$wf/workflow.toml"
196	  git -C "$repo" add -A
197	  git -C "$repo" commit -qm "perf harness seed"
198	  PERF_REPOS+=("$repo")
199	  PERF_REPO="$repo"
200	}
201	
202	# --- daemon control --------------------------------------------------------
203	
204	perf_descriptor_field() {
205	  local dd="$1" field="$2"
206	  [ -f "$dd/runtime.json" ] || return 1
207	  jq -r --arg f "$field" '.[$f] // empty' "$dd/runtime.json" 2>/dev/null
208	}
209	
210	# perf_daemon_start <data-dir> [fake-script] [ready-timeout-s]
211	#
212	# Spawns `sgt daemon` detached in its own session with the given
213	# SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT (empty = the fake's default: every stage completes), then
214	# waits for the documented client handshake — the runtime descriptor plus a
215	# healthy /healthz — and exports:
216	#
217	#   PERF_DAEMON_PID  PERF_ENDPOINT  PERF_TOKEN  PERF_DATA_DIR
218	#   PERF_DAEMON_START_NS  PERF_DAEMON_READY_NS  PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS
219	#
220	# PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS is the cold-start figure S5 reports: spawn to first
221	# answered request, which is journal replay + registry fold + DuckDB rebuild +
222	# listener bind.
223	perf_daemon_start() {
224	  local dd="$1" script="${2:-}" timeout="${3:-300}"
225	  mkdir -p "$dd"
226	  PERF_DATA_DIR="$dd"
227	  rm -f "$dd/runtime.json"
228	  local log="$dd/daemon.stdio.log"
229	  local t0 t1
230	  perf_mark t0
231	  if [ -n "$script" ]; then
232	    SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT="$script" setsid "$SGT_BIN" daemon --data-dir "$dd" >>"$log" 2>&1 &
233	  else
234	    env -u SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT setsid "$SGT_BIN" daemon --data-dir "$dd" >>"$log" 2>&1 &
235	  fi
236	  # `setsid` forks when the caller is already a process-group leader, so the
237	  # job's pid is not necessarily the daemon's. The descriptor is authoritative:
238	  # the daemon writes its own pid there, after the listener is live.
239	  local start_s=$SECONDS
240	  local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout)) endpoint="" token="" pid=""
241	  while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
242	    if [ -f "$dd/runtime.json" ]; then
243	      endpoint="$(perf_descriptor_field "$dd" endpoint || true)"
244	      token="$(perf_descriptor_field "$dd" token || true)"
245	      pid="$(perf_descriptor_field "$dd" pid || true)"
246	      if [ -n "$endpoint" ] && [ -n "$token" ] && [ -n "$pid" ]; then
247	        if curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$endpoint/healthz" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 200; then
248	          break
249	        fi
250	      fi
251	    fi
252	    # Fail fast on a daemon that died instead of waiting out the whole
253	    # timeout: after a grace period, no process for this data dir means the
254	    # start failed and the log already says why.
255	    if [ $((SECONDS - start_s)) -ge 10 ] && ! pgrep -f "sgt daemon --data-dir $dd" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
256	      break
257	    fi
258	    sleep 0.02
259	  done
260	  perf_mark t1
261	  if [ -z "$endpoint" ]; then
262	    perf_warn "daemon log tail:"; tail -20 "$log" >&2 || true
263	    perf_die "daemon never published a usable descriptor for $dd"
264	  fi
265	  PERF_DAEMON_PID="$pid"
266	  PERF_ENDPOINT="$endpoint"
267	  PERF_TOKEN="$token"
268	  PERF_DAEMON_START_NS="$t0"
269	  PERF_DAEMON_READY_NS="$t1"
270	  PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS="$(perf_ms $((t1 - t0)))"
271	  PERF_FAKE_SCRIPT_IN_USE="$script"
272	}
273	
274	# perf_empty_start_ms <scratch-base> [samples]
275	#
276	# Cold start of a daemon on a brand-new *empty* data dir, best of N. This is
277	# the fixed overhead every start pays — exec, DuckDB open, bind, descriptor —
278	# and it is what has to be subtracted from a loaded cold start before the
279	# remainder can be called "replay". Measured next to the loaded start rather
280	# than once per run, because a single sample taken minutes earlier on a busy
281	# container is not the same machine.
282	#
283	# The caller's current daemon coordinates are saved and restored, so this can
284	# be called from inside a scenario without losing track of its daemon.
285	perf_empty_start_ms() {
286	  local base="$1" samples="${2:-2}" best="" i tmpdd ms
287	  local save_pid="${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" save_ep="${PERF_ENDPOINT:-}"
288	  local save_tok="${PERF_TOKEN:-}" save_dd="${PERF_DATA_DIR:-}"
289	  for ((i = 1; i <= samples; i++)); do
290	    tmpdd="$base/empty-start-$i"
291	    rm -rf "$tmpdd"; mkdir -p "$tmpdd"
292	    perf_daemon_start "$tmpdd"
293	    ms="$PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS"
294	    perf_daemon_stop
295	    rm -rf "$tmpdd"
296	    best="$(awk -v a="$best" -v b="$ms" 'BEGIN{ if (a == "" || b + 0 < a + 0) print b; else print a }')"
297	  done
298	  PERF_DAEMON_PID="$save_pid"; PERF_ENDPOINT="$save_ep"
299	  PERF_TOKEN="$save_tok"; PERF_DATA_DIR="$save_dd"
300	  printf '%s' "$best"
301	}
302	
303	# perf_daemon_stop [pid] [timeout-s] — SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if it will not go.
304	# Sets PERF_FORCE_KILLED=1 (and warns) when SIGKILL was needed: that is a
305	# finding, not a cleanup detail.
306	perf_daemon_stop() {
307	  local pid="${1:-${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}}" timeout="${2:-20}" i
308	  [ -n "$pid" ] || return 0
309	  kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || { PERF_DAEMON_PID=""; return 0; }
310	  kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
311	  for ((i = 0; i < timeout * 20; i++)); do
312	    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
313	    sleep 0.05
314	  done
315	  if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
316	    perf_warn "daemon $pid ignored SIGTERM for ${timeout}s — SIGKILL"
317	    kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
318	    PERF_FORCE_KILLED=1
319	    sleep 0.3
320	  fi
321	  [ "$pid" = "${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" ] && PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
322	  return 0
323	}
324	
325	# perf_daemon_kill9 [pid] — the S6 crash: no chance to shut down cleanly.
326	perf_daemon_kill9() {
327	  local pid="${1:-${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}}"
328	  [ -n "$pid" ] || return 0
329	  kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
330	  local i
331	  for ((i = 0; i < 200; i++)); do
332	    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
333	    sleep 0.05
334	  done
335	  [ "$pid" = "${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" ] && PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
336	  return 0
337	}
338	
339	# --- /proc sampling --------------------------------------------------------
340	
341	PERF_SAMPLE_HEADER='ts_ns,rss_kb,hwm_kb,threads,fds,utime_ticks,stime_ticks,cpu_sec,label'
342	
343	# perf_sample_row <pid> [label] — one CSV row from /proc/<pid>/{status,stat,fd}.
344	# Prints nothing and returns 1 if the process is gone (a sampler must not die
345	# because the thing it samples did).
346	perf_sample_row() {
347	  local pid="$1" label="${2:-}"
348	  [ -d "/proc/$pid" ] || return 1
349	  local rss=0 hwm=0 thr=0 line
350	  while IFS= read -r line; do
351	    case "$line" in
352	      VmRSS:*) rss="${line//[!0-9]/}" ;;
353	      VmHWM:*) hwm="${line//[!0-9]/}" ;;
354	      Threads:*) thr="${line//[!0-9]/}" ;;
355	    esac
356	  done < "/proc/$pid/status" 2>/dev/null || return 1
357	  local stat rest fields utime=0 stime=0
358	  stat="$(< "/proc/$pid/stat")" 2>/dev/null || return 1
359	  rest="${stat#*') '}"
360	  read -ra fields <<< "$rest"
361	  # After the comm field, index 0 is stat field 3; utime is field 14, stime 15.
362	  utime="${fields[11]:-0}"
363	  stime="${fields[12]:-0}"
364	  local fds=0 entries
365	  entries=(/proc/"$pid"/fd/*)
366	  if [ -e "${entries[0]}" ]; then fds="${#entries[@]}"; fi
367	  local cpu
368	  cpu="$(awk -v u="$utime" -v s="$stime" -v t="$PERF_CLK_TCK" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", (u+s)/t}')"
369	  printf '%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s\n' \
370	    "$(perf_now_ns)" "$rss" "$hwm" "$thr" "$fds" "$utime" "$stime" "$cpu" "$label"
371	}
372	
373	# perf_sampler_start <pid> <csv> [interval-s] [label]
374	perf_sampler_start() {
375	  local pid="$1" csv="$2" interval="${3:-0.5}" label="${4:-}"
376	  echo "$PERF_SAMPLE_HEADER" > "$csv"
377	  (
378	    while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
379	      perf_sample_row "$pid" "$label" >> "$csv" 2>/dev/null || true
380	      sleep "$interval"
381	    done
382	  ) &
383	  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=$!
384	}
385	
386	perf_sampler_stop() {
387	  [ -n "${PERF_SAMPLER_PID:-}" ] || return 0
388	  kill "$PERF_SAMPLER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
389	  wait "$PERF_SAMPLER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
390	  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=""
391	  return 0
392	}
393	
394	# perf_sample_stats <csv> — "peak_rss_kb peak_hwm_kb max_fds max_threads
395	# last_cpu_sec first_rss_kb last_rss_kb samples" from a sampler CSV.
396	perf_sample_stats() {
397	  python3 - "$1" <<'PY'
398	import csv, sys
399	rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(sys.argv[1])))
400	rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("rss_kb")]
401	if not rows:
402	    print("0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0"); raise SystemExit
403	i = lambda r, k: int(r[k] or 0)
404	print(max(i(r, "rss_kb") for r in rows),
405	      max(i(r, "hwm_kb") for r in rows),
406	      max(i(r, "fds") for r in rows),
407	      max(i(r, "threads") for r in rows),
408	      rows[-1]["cpu_sec"],
409	      i(rows[0], "rss_kb"),
410	      i(rows[-1], "rss_kb"),
411	      len(rows))
412	PY
413	}
414	
415	# perf_proc_rss <pid> — VmRSS in kB, or 0.
416	perf_proc_rss() {
417	  local line
418	  while IFS= read -r line; do
419	    case "$line" in VmRSS:*) echo "${line//[!0-9]/}"; return 0 ;; esac
420	  done < "/proc/$1/status" 2>/dev/null
421	  echo 0
422	}
423	perf_proc_hwm() {
424	  local line
425	  while IFS= read -r line; do
426	    case "$line" in VmHWM:*) echo "${line//[!0-9]/}"; return 0 ;; esac
427	  done < "/proc/$1/status" 2>/dev/null
428	  echo 0
429	}
430	perf_proc_cpu_sec() {
431	  local stat rest fields
432	  stat="$(< "/proc/$1/stat")" 2>/dev/null || { echo 0; return 0; }
433	  rest="${stat#*') '}"
434	  read -ra fields <<< "$rest"
435	  awk -v u="${fields[11]:-0}" -v s="${fields[12]:-0}" -v t="$PERF_CLK_TCK" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", (u+s)/t}'
436	}
437	perf_proc_fds() {
438	  local entries
439	  entries=(/proc/"$1"/fd/*)
440	  if [ -e "${entries[0]}" ]; then echo "${#entries[@]}"; else echo 0; fi
441	}
442	
443	# --- API driving -----------------------------------------------------------
444	
445	PERF_ULID_ALPHABET=0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ
446	
447	# A syntactically valid ULID (26 Crockford base32 chars, first char <= '7' so
448	# the 48-bit timestamp cannot overflow). The daemon only validates the shape.
449	perf_ulid() {
450	  local out="${PERF_ULID_ALPHABET:$((RANDOM % 8)):1}" i
451	  for ((i = 0; i < 25; i++)); do out+="${PERF_ULID_ALPHABET:$((RANDOM % 32)):1}"; done
452	  printf '%s' "$out"
453	}
454	
455	perf_api() { # perf_api <method> <path> [json-body]
456	  local method="$1" path="$2" body="${3:-}"
457	  if [ -n "$body" ]; then
458	    curl -sS -m "${PERF_HTTP_TIMEOUT:-300}" -X "$method" \
459	      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERF_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
460	      -d "$body" "$PERF_ENDPOINT$path"
461	  else
462	    curl -sS -m "${PERF_HTTP_TIMEOUT:-300}" -X "$method" \
463	      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERF_TOKEN" "$PERF_ENDPOINT$path"
464	  fi
465	}
466	
467	# perf_timed_get <path> <outfile> — GET timed with curl's own clock.
468	# Prints "wall_ns http_code bytes curl_total_s".
469	perf_timed_get() {
470	  local path="$1" out="${2:-/dev/null}" t0 t1 line
471	  perf_mark t0
472	  line="$(curl -sS -m "${PERF_HTTP_TIMEOUT:-300}" -o "$out" \
473	    -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}' \
474	    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERF_TOKEN" "$PERF_ENDPOINT$path" 2>/dev/null)"
475	  perf_mark t1
476	  printf '%s %s\n' "$((t1 - t0))" "$line"
477	}
478	
479	# perf_submit <intent> [cwd] [backend] — one synchronous submit; prints the
480	# work id (empty on failure). Body is built before the clock starts.
481	perf_submit() {
482	  local intent="$1" cwd="${2:-${PERF_REPO:-}}" backend="${3:-fake}" body resp
483	  body="$(jq -nc --arg cid "$(perf_ulid)" --arg intent "$intent" --arg cwd "$cwd" --arg b "$backend" \
484	    '{command_id:$cid, intent:$intent, backend:$b, origin:{client:"cli", cwd:$cwd}}')"
485	  resp="$(perf_api POST /v1/work "$body")"
486	  jq -r '.work.id // empty' <<< "$resp"
487	}
488	
489	# perf_respond <work-id> <input> — prints the resulting work state.
490	perf_respond() {
491	  local id="$1" input="$2" body resp
492	  body="$(jq -nc --arg cid "$(perf_ulid)" --arg i "$input" '{command_id:$cid, input:$i}')"
493	  resp="$(perf_api POST "/v1/work/$id/input" "$body")"
494	  jq -r '.work.state // .error.code // "?"' <<< "$resp"
495	}
496	
497	perf_cancel() {
498	  local id="$1" body
499	  body="$(jq -nc --arg cid "$(perf_ulid)" '{command_id:$cid}')"
500	  perf_api POST "/v1/work/$id/cancel" "$body" > /dev/null
501	}
502	
503	perf_work_state() { perf_api GET "/v1/work/$1" | jq -r '.work.state // "?"'; }
504	
505	perf_journal_head() { perf_api GET /v1/system | jq -r '.journal_head // 0'; }
506	
507	perf_state_counts() { # "state:count" lines over the whole fleet
508	  perf_api GET /v1/work | jq -r '[.works[].state] | group_by(.) | map({(.[0]): length}) | add // {} | to_entries[] | "\(.key):\(.value)"'
509	}
510	
511	perf_count_state() { perf_api GET /v1/work | jq --arg s "$1" '[.works[] | select(.state == $s)] | length'; }
512	
513	perf_journal_events() { # events on disk, independent of the daemon
514	  local dd="${1:-$PERF_DATA_DIR}"
515	  cat "$dd"/journal/*.ndjson 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
516	}
517	
518	# perf_burst <n> <parallel> <calls-dir> [intent-prefix]
519	#
520	# n concurrent submits through the HTTP API (one curl per call, xargs -P for
521	# fan-out) writing one CSV line per call into <calls-dir>. The submit path
522	# runs the whole workflow inside the request with the fake backend, so a call's
523	# latency is a work's end-to-end latency.
524	perf_burst() {
525	  local n="$1" par="$2" dir="$3" prefix="${4:-perf}"
526	  mkdir -p "$dir"
527	  seq 1 "$n" | xargs -P "$par" -I@ \
528	    "$PERF_DIR/_submit-one.sh" "$PERF_ENDPOINT" "$PERF_TOKEN" "${PERF_REPO:-}" "$prefix-@" "$dir/@.csv"
529	}
530	
531	# perf_collect_calls <calls-dir> <out-csv> — concatenate per-call CSVs.
532	perf_collect_calls() {
533	  local dir="$1" out="$2"
534	  echo 't_start_ns,wall_ns,curl_total_s,http_code,work_id,state' > "$out"
535	  cat "$dir"/*.csv 2>/dev/null >> "$out" || true
536	}
537	
538	# --- statistics ------------------------------------------------------------
539	
540	# perf_pctl — numbers on stdin, prints "count min p50 p95 p99 max mean".
541	#
542	# `python3 -c`, not a heredoc: a heredoc *is* python's stdin, which would eat
543	# the numbers being piped in (this cost one silent run of all-zero latency
544	# columns before it was caught).
545	perf_pctl() {
546	  python3 -c '
547	import sys
548	xs = sorted(float(x) for x in sys.stdin.read().split() if x.strip())
549	if not xs:
550	    print("0 0 0 0 0 0 0"); raise SystemExit
551	def p(q):
552	    if len(xs) == 1: return xs[0]
553	    k = q * (len(xs) - 1)
554	    lo, hi = int(k), min(int(k) + 1, len(xs) - 1)
555	    return xs[lo] + (xs[hi] - xs[lo]) * (k - lo)
556	print(len(xs), "%.3f" % xs[0], "%.3f" % p(.5), "%.3f" % p(.95), "%.3f" % p(.99),
557	      "%.3f" % xs[-1], "%.3f" % (sum(xs) / len(xs)))
558	'
559	}
560	
561	perf_ms() { awk -v n="$1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", n/1000000}'; }
562	perf_s()  { awk -v n="$1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", n/1000000000}'; }
563	
564	# perf_latency_kv <prefix> <csv> <column-index-1based>
565	# Emits <prefix>_{count,min_ms,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,max_ms,mean_ms} from a
566	# calls CSV whose column holds nanoseconds.
567	perf_latency_kv() {
568	  local prefix="$1" csv="$2" col="${3:-2}" stats
569	  stats="$(tail -n +2 "$csv" | cut -d, -f"$col" | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | awk '{printf "%.3f\n", $1/1000000}' | perf_pctl)"
570	  read -r c mn p50 p95 p99 mx mean <<< "$stats"
571	  perf_kv "${prefix}_count" "$c"
572	  perf_kv "${prefix}_min_ms" "$mn"
573	  perf_kv "${prefix}_p50_ms" "$p50"
574	  perf_kv "${prefix}_p95_ms" "$p95"
575	  perf_kv "${prefix}_p99_ms" "$p99"
576	  perf_kv "${prefix}_max_ms" "$mx"
577	  perf_kv "${prefix}_mean_ms" "$mean"
578	}
579	
580	# --- disk accounting -------------------------------------------------------
581	
582	perf_bytes() { du -sb "$1" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 || echo 0; }
583	
584	perf_disk_kv() { # perf_disk_kv <prefix> <data-dir>
585	  local prefix="$1" dd="$2"
586	  perf_kv "${prefix}_total_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd")"
587	  perf_kv "${prefix}_journal_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd/journal")"
588	  perf_kv "${prefix}_blobs_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd/blobs")"
589	  perf_kv "${prefix}_surfaces_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd/surfaces")"
590	  perf_kv "${prefix}_duckdb_bytes" "$(stat -c %s "$dd/projections/sergeant.duckdb" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
591	}
592	
593	# --- hygiene sweep ---------------------------------------------------------
594	
595	# perf_sgt_processes — sgt processes visible right now, one per line, with this
596	# harness's own shell and pgrep invocations filtered out. Never fails: pgrep
597	# and grep both exit 1 on "no matches", which under `set -o pipefail` would
598	# otherwise abort the caller.
599	perf_sgt_processes() {
600	  { pgrep -fa "release/sgt" 2>/dev/null; pgrep -fa "debug/sgt" 2>/dev/null; } \
601	    | grep -v "bash -c" | grep -v "scripts/perf" | grep -v "pgrep" || true
602	}
603	
604	perf_sgt_process_count() {
605	  local list; list="$(perf_sgt_processes)"
606	  if [ -z "$list" ]; then echo 0; else printf '%s\n' "$list" | wc -l | tr -d ' '; fi
607	}
608	
609	
610	# perf_hygiene <label> [repo...] — the sweep P1-PERF ends every scenario with.
611	# Writes hygiene-<label>.txt and prints the verdict. Never exits nonzero: a
612	# dirty sweep is data the scenario must report, not a reason to abort.
613	perf_hygiene() {
614	  local label="$1"; shift
615	  local file="${PERF_OUT:-.}/hygiene-${label}.txt"
616	  local orphans strays worktrees=0 repo verdict=clean
617	  # Repos may arrive both as arguments and in PERF_REPOS; count each once.
618	  local repos=() seen existing
619	  for repo in "$@" "${PERF_REPOS[@]:-}"; do
620	    [ -n "$repo" ] && [ -d "$repo/.git" ] || continue
621	    seen=no
622	    for existing in "${repos[@]:-}"; do [ "$existing" = "$repo" ] && seen=yes; done
623	    [ "$seen" = no ] && repos+=("$repo")
624	  done
625	  # pgrep's own invocation is wrapped in a `bash -c` whose command line holds
626	  # the pattern; that self-match is filtered, nothing else is.
627	  orphans="$(perf_sgt_processes)"
628	  strays="$(ls -d /tmp/.tmp* /tmp/sgt-demo-* "/tmp/tmux-$(id -u)"/sgtperf-* 2>/dev/null || true)"
629	  {
630	    echo "hygiene sweep: $label   ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
631	    echo "-- sgt processes"
632	    if [ -n "$orphans" ]; then echo "$orphans"; else echo "(none)"; fi
633	    echo "-- /tmp residue (.tmp*, sgt-demo-*, stale sgtperf tmux sockets)"
634	    if [ -n "$strays" ]; then echo "$strays"; else echo "(none)"; fi
635	    echo "-- worktrees"
636	    echo "   (a worktree under <data-dir>/surfaces/<work-id>/ belongs to that"
637	    echo "    work and is expected while the work is non-terminal: teardown"
638	    echo "    retires a surface only when the work reaches a terminal state.)"
639	    for repo in "${repos[@]:-}"; do
640	      echo "[$repo]"
641	      git -C "$repo" worktree list 2>/dev/null || true
642	    done
643	    echo "-- surfaces dirs"
644	    if [ -n "${PERF_DATA_DIR:-}" ] && [ -d "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" ]; then
645	      find "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 2>/dev/null || true
646	    else
647	      echo "(no surfaces dir)"
648	    fi
649	  } > "$file"
650	  local n
651	  for repo in "${repos[@]:-}"; do
652	    n="$(git -C "$repo" worktree list 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
653	    worktrees=$((worktrees + n))
654	  done
655	  local nproc_left=0
656	  [ -n "$orphans" ] && nproc_left="$(printf '%s\n' "$orphans" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
657	  # Surfaces are counted in two buckets, because they mean different things:
658	  # a *populated* surface dir is a worktree that outlived its work (dirty), an
659	  # *empty* one is a directory teardown did not remove. Measured separately so
660	  # the second is reportable as its own finding instead of being lost inside a
661	  # "dirty" verdict.
662	  local nsurf=0 nsurf_nonempty=0 d
663	  if [ -n "${PERF_DATA_DIR:-}" ] && [ -d "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" ]; then
664	    while IFS= read -r d; do
665	      [ -n "$d" ] || continue
666	      nsurf=$((nsurf + 1))
667	      [ -n "$(ls -A "$d" 2>/dev/null)" ] && nsurf_nonempty=$((nsurf_nonempty + 1))
668	    done < <(find "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d 2>/dev/null)
669	  fi
670	  [ "$nproc_left" -eq 0 ] && [ "$worktrees" -eq 0 ] && [ "$nsurf_nonempty" -eq 0 ] || verdict=dirty
671	  perf_say "hygiene[$label]: $verdict — sgt procs=$nproc_left stray worktrees=$worktrees populated surfaces=$nsurf_nonempty empty surface dirs=$((nsurf - nsurf_nonempty)) (detail: $file)"
672	  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_verdict" "$verdict"
673	  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_sgt_processes" "$nproc_left"
674	  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_worktrees" "$worktrees"
675	  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs" "$nsurf"
676	  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs_populated" "$nsurf_nonempty"
677	  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs_empty_leftover" "$((nsurf - nsurf_nonempty))"
678	  local nstray=0
679	  [ -n "$strays" ] && nstray="$(printf '%s\n' "$strays" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
680	  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_tmp_residue" "$nstray"
681	  return 0
682	}
683	
684	# --- environment record ----------------------------------------------------
685	
686	perf_environment() { # perf_environment <outfile>
687	  local out="$1"
688	  {
689	    echo "commit: ${PERF_COMMIT:-unknown}"
690	    echo "binary: $SGT_BIN"
691	    echo "sgt --version: $("$SGT_BIN" --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
692	    echo "nproc: $(nproc)"
693	    echo "cgroup cpu.max: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max 2>/dev/null || echo 'absent (cgroup v1)')"
694	    echo "cgroup v1 cfs_quota_us: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"
695	    echo "cgroup v1 cfs_period_us: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"
696	    echo "MemTotal: $(awk '/MemTotal/{print $2" kB"}' /proc/meminfo)"
697	    echo "kernel: $(uname -sr)"
698	    echo "CLK_TCK: $PERF_CLK_TCK"
699	    echo "df (output mount):"
700	    df -h "${PERF_OUT:-.}" | sed 's/^/  /'
701	    echo "ulimit -n: $(ulimit -n)"
702	  } | tee "$out"
703	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/perf/common.sh — shared helpers for the P1-PERF load/stress harness.
#
# Sourced by every s*-*.sh scenario and by run-all.sh. Nothing here measures
# anything on its own; it supplies the four things every scenario needs:
#
#   * a scenario workspace   — fresh data dir + a seeded git repo (demo.sh's
#                              recipe: .sergeant/workflows/<name>/<stage>/)
#   * a daemon under control — spawned with a chosen SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT, its pid
#                              read from the runtime descriptor (the documented
#                              client handshake), stopped and verified stopped
#   * /proc sampling         — VmRSS / VmHWM / threads / fd count / utime+stime
#                              into CSV, either one row on demand or a
#                              background sampler at a chosen interval
#   * measurement plumbing   — latency timing, percentiles, a summary block
#                              that is printed and written as JSON, and the
#                              hygiene sweep
#
# The harness drives the shipped release binary and its loopback HTTP API and
# adds no Rust (P1-PERF non-goal: "new Rust code beyond what a scenario
# strictly needs"). High-rate cells drive POST /v1/... with curl rather than
# one CLI process per call, because the CLI spawns a process per call and that
# is the client's cost, not the daemon's.
#
# Nothing under here writes into the repository tree: every scenario's data
# dirs, repos and raw output live under the <outdir> it is given.

# --- resolution ------------------------------------------------------------

PERF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PERF_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$PERF_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# The unit under test is the release build (P1-PERF: "the baseline describes
# what ships, not debug-profile DuckDB").
SGT_BIN="${SGT_BIN:-$PERF_REPO_ROOT/target/release/sgt}"

PERF_CLK_TCK="$(getconf CLK_TCK 2>/dev/null || echo 100)"

# Timing: CLOCK_REALTIME nanoseconds. `date +%s%N` costs a fork (~2 ms on this
# container) which is the same order as the thing being measured, so the
# fork-free bash-5 EPOCHREALTIME is preferred and `date` is the fallback. Same
# clock, same units.
perf_now_ns() {
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    printf '%s%s\n' "$sec" "${frac:0:9}"
  else
    date +%s%N
  fi
}

# perf_mark VAR — assign "now" in ns to VAR without forking a subshell.
perf_mark() {
  local -n __perf_mark_out=$1
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    __perf_mark_out="${sec}${frac:0:9}"
  else
    __perf_mark_out="$(date +%s%N)"
  fi
}

perf_die() { printf '\033[31mperf: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
perf_say() { printf '   %s\n' "$*"; }
perf_step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
perf_warn() { printf '\033[33m   ! %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; }

perf_require_binary() {
  [ -x "$SGT_BIN" ] || perf_die "no release binary at $SGT_BIN (cargo build --release)"
  for tool in curl jq python3 git; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || perf_die "missing required tool: $tool"
  done
  # The tested binary's identity, captured exactly once — a live rev-parse per
  # scenario tracks the checkout, not the binary: a commit landing mid-matrix
  # made 6 of 8 scenarios self-report code that was never in the binary
  # (issue #50). Exported so scenarios spawned by run-all.sh inherit the pin
  # instead of re-reading HEAD.
  if [ -z "${PERF_COMMIT:-}" ]; then
    PERF_COMMIT="$(git -C "$PERF_REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    export PERF_COMMIT
  fi
}

# --- scenario lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------

# perf_init <outdir> <scenario-name>
#
# Creates the output dir, the scenario's scratch dir (data dirs and seed repos
# live there, never in the repo tree), opens the summary accumulator, and
# installs the teardown trap so an aborted scenario still stops its daemon.
perf_init() {
  PERF_OUT="$1"
  PERF_SCENARIO="$2"
  perf_require_binary
  mkdir -p "$PERF_OUT"
  PERF_OUT="$(cd "$PERF_OUT" && pwd)"
  PERF_SCRATCH="$PERF_OUT/scratch"
  mkdir -p "$PERF_SCRATCH"
  PERF_SUMMARY_TSV="$PERF_OUT/${PERF_SCENARIO}-summary.tsv"
  : > "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV"
  PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=""
  PERF_FORCE_KILLED=0
  PERF_REPOS=()
  PERF_START_NS="$(perf_now_ns)"
  trap 'perf_teardown' EXIT
  perf_step "$PERF_SCENARIO — output $PERF_OUT"
  perf_kv scenario "$PERF_SCENARIO"
  perf_kv binary "$SGT_BIN"
  perf_kv commit "$PERF_COMMIT"
  perf_kv started_at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
}

perf_teardown() {
  local rc=$?
  perf_sampler_stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if [ -n "${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" ] && kill -0 "$PERF_DAEMON_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    perf_daemon_stop "$PERF_DAEMON_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  return $rc
}

# --- the summary block -----------------------------------------------------

# perf_kv <key> <value> — one distilled measurement.
perf_kv() { printf '%s\t%s\n' "$1" "$2" >> "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV"; }

# perf_summary — print the distilled block and write <scenario>-summary.json.
perf_summary() {
  python3 - "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV" "$PERF_OUT/${PERF_SCENARIO}-summary.json" "$PERF_SCENARIO" <<'PY'
import json, sys
tsv, out, name = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
rows = []
for line in open(tsv):
    line = line.rstrip("\n")
    if not line:
        continue
    key, _, value = line.partition("\t")
    rows.append((key, value))
doc = {}
for key, value in rows:
    try:
        doc[key] = int(value)
    except ValueError:
        try:
            doc[key] = float(value)
        except ValueError:
            doc[key] = value
json.dump(doc, open(out, "w"), indent=2, sort_keys=False)
width = max((len(k) for k, _ in rows), default=0)
print()
print(f"\033[1m-- {name} summary " + "-" * max(0, 58 - len(name)) + "\033[0m")
for key, value in rows:
    print(f"   {key.ljust(width)}  {value}")
print(f"   (json: {out})")
PY
}

# --- seed repo (demo.sh's recipe) ------------------------------------------

# perf_seed_repo <repo-dir> [stage-count]
#
# A throwaway git repository carrying a `.sergeant/workflows/software-change`
# workflow — the same layout scripts/demo.sh builds, which is what makes the
# submit path materialize a surface and run stages instead of parking the work
# in `pending`.
perf_seed_repo() {
  local repo="$1" stages="${2:-2}"
  mkdir -p "$repo"
  git init -q -b main "$repo"
  git -C "$repo" config user.email perf@example.invalid
  git -C "$repo" config user.name "sgt perf harness"
  git -C "$repo" config commit.gpgsign false
  printf 'def settle(payment):\n    return gateway.settle(payment)\n' > "$repo/payments.py"
  local wf="$repo/.sergeant/workflows/software-change"
  mkdir -p "$wf"
  local names=(10-implement 20-review 30-verify 40-land 50-followup)
  local ids=() i id
  for ((i = 0; i < stages; i++)); do
    if [ "$i" -lt "${#names[@]}" ]; then id="${names[$i]}"; else id="$(printf '%02d-stage%d' $(((i + 1) * 10)) $((i + 1)))"; fi
    ids+=("$id")
    mkdir -p "$wf/$id"
    printf 'Stage %s of the perf workflow.\n' "$id" > "$wf/$id/CONTEXT.md"
  done
  {
    printf '[workflow]\nname = "software-change"\nversion = "1"\nstages = ['
    local sep=""
    for id in "${ids[@]}"; do printf '%s"%s"' "$sep" "$id"; sep=", "; done
    printf ']\n'
  } > "$wf/workflow.toml"
  git -C "$repo" add -A
  git -C "$repo" commit -qm "perf harness seed"
  PERF_REPOS+=("$repo")
  PERF_REPO="$repo"
}

# --- daemon control --------------------------------------------------------

perf_descriptor_field() {
  local dd="$1" field="$2"
  [ -f "$dd/runtime.json" ] || return 1
  jq -r --arg f "$field" '.[$f] // empty' "$dd/runtime.json" 2>/dev/null
}

# perf_daemon_start <data-dir> [fake-script] [ready-timeout-s]
#
# Spawns `sgt daemon` detached in its own session with the given
# SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT (empty = the fake's default: every stage completes), then
# waits for the documented client handshake — the runtime descriptor plus a
# healthy /healthz — and exports:
#
#   PERF_DAEMON_PID  PERF_ENDPOINT  PERF_TOKEN  PERF_DATA_DIR
#   PERF_DAEMON_START_NS  PERF_DAEMON_READY_NS  PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS
#
# PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS is the cold-start figure S5 reports: spawn to first
# answered request, which is journal replay + registry fold + DuckDB rebuild +
# listener bind.
perf_daemon_start() {
  local dd="$1" script="${2:-}" timeout="${3:-300}"
  mkdir -p "$dd"
  PERF_DATA_DIR="$dd"
  rm -f "$dd/runtime.json"
  local log="$dd/daemon.stdio.log"
  local t0 t1
  perf_mark t0
  if [ -n "$script" ]; then
    SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT="$script" setsid "$SGT_BIN" daemon --data-dir "$dd" >>"$log" 2>&1 &
  else
    env -u SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT setsid "$SGT_BIN" daemon --data-dir "$dd" >>"$log" 2>&1 &
  fi
  # `setsid` forks when the caller is already a process-group leader, so the
  # job's pid is not necessarily the daemon's. The descriptor is authoritative:
  # the daemon writes its own pid there, after the listener is live.
  local start_s=$SECONDS
  local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout)) endpoint="" token="" pid=""
  while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$deadline" ]; do
    if [ -f "$dd/runtime.json" ]; then
      endpoint="$(perf_descriptor_field "$dd" endpoint || true)"
      token="$(perf_descriptor_field "$dd" token || true)"
      pid="$(perf_descriptor_field "$dd" pid || true)"
      if [ -n "$endpoint" ] && [ -n "$token" ] && [ -n "$pid" ]; then
        if curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$endpoint/healthz" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 200; then
          break
        fi
      fi
    fi
    # Fail fast on a daemon that died instead of waiting out the whole
    # timeout: after a grace period, no process for this data dir means the
    # start failed and the log already says why.
    if [ $((SECONDS - start_s)) -ge 10 ] && ! pgrep -f "sgt daemon --data-dir $dd" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
      break
    fi
    sleep 0.02
  done
  perf_mark t1
  if [ -z "$endpoint" ]; then
    perf_warn "daemon log tail:"; tail -20 "$log" >&2 || true
    perf_die "daemon never published a usable descriptor for $dd"
  fi
  PERF_DAEMON_PID="$pid"
  PERF_ENDPOINT="$endpoint"
  PERF_TOKEN="$token"
  PERF_DAEMON_START_NS="$t0"
  PERF_DAEMON_READY_NS="$t1"
  PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS="$(perf_ms $((t1 - t0)))"
  PERF_FAKE_SCRIPT_IN_USE="$script"
}

# perf_empty_start_ms <scratch-base> [samples]
#
# Cold start of a daemon on a brand-new *empty* data dir, best of N. This is
# the fixed overhead every start pays — exec, DuckDB open, bind, descriptor —
# and it is what has to be subtracted from a loaded cold start before the
# remainder can be called "replay". Measured next to the loaded start rather
# than once per run, because a single sample taken minutes earlier on a busy
# container is not the same machine.
#
# The caller's current daemon coordinates are saved and restored, so this can
# be called from inside a scenario without losing track of its daemon.
perf_empty_start_ms() {
  local base="$1" samples="${2:-2}" best="" i tmpdd ms
  local save_pid="${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" save_ep="${PERF_ENDPOINT:-}"
  local save_tok="${PERF_TOKEN:-}" save_dd="${PERF_DATA_DIR:-}"
  for ((i = 1; i <= samples; i++)); do
    tmpdd="$base/empty-start-$i"
    rm -rf "$tmpdd"; mkdir -p "$tmpdd"
    perf_daemon_start "$tmpdd"
    ms="$PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS"
    perf_daemon_stop
    rm -rf "$tmpdd"
    best="$(awk -v a="$best" -v b="$ms" 'BEGIN{ if (a == "" || b + 0 < a + 0) print b; else print a }')"
  done
  PERF_DAEMON_PID="$save_pid"; PERF_ENDPOINT="$save_ep"
  PERF_TOKEN="$save_tok"; PERF_DATA_DIR="$save_dd"
  printf '%s' "$best"
}

# perf_daemon_stop [pid] [timeout-s] — SIGTERM, then SIGKILL if it will not go.
# Sets PERF_FORCE_KILLED=1 (and warns) when SIGKILL was needed: that is a
# finding, not a cleanup detail.
perf_daemon_stop() {
  local pid="${1:-${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}}" timeout="${2:-20}" i
  [ -n "$pid" ] || return 0
  kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || { PERF_DAEMON_PID=""; return 0; }
  kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  for ((i = 0; i < timeout * 20; i++)); do
    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    sleep 0.05
  done
  if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    perf_warn "daemon $pid ignored SIGTERM for ${timeout}s — SIGKILL"
    kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    PERF_FORCE_KILLED=1
    sleep 0.3
  fi
  [ "$pid" = "${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" ] && PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
  return 0
}

# perf_daemon_kill9 [pid] — the S6 crash: no chance to shut down cleanly.
perf_daemon_kill9() {
  local pid="${1:-${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}}"
  [ -n "$pid" ] || return 0
  kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  local i
  for ((i = 0; i < 200; i++)); do
    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    sleep 0.05
  done
  [ "$pid" = "${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" ] && PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
  return 0
}

# --- /proc sampling --------------------------------------------------------

PERF_SAMPLE_HEADER='ts_ns,rss_kb,hwm_kb,threads,fds,utime_ticks,stime_ticks,cpu_sec,label'

# perf_sample_row <pid> [label] — one CSV row from /proc/<pid>/{status,stat,fd}.
# Prints nothing and returns 1 if the process is gone (a sampler must not die
# because the thing it samples did).
perf_sample_row() {
  local pid="$1" label="${2:-}"
  [ -d "/proc/$pid" ] || return 1
  local rss=0 hwm=0 thr=0 line
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in
      VmRSS:*) rss="${line//[!0-9]/}" ;;
      VmHWM:*) hwm="${line//[!0-9]/}" ;;
      Threads:*) thr="${line//[!0-9]/}" ;;
    esac
  done < "/proc/$pid/status" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  local stat rest fields utime=0 stime=0
  stat="$(< "/proc/$pid/stat")" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  rest="${stat#*') '}"
  read -ra fields <<< "$rest"
  # After the comm field, index 0 is stat field 3; utime is field 14, stime 15.
  utime="${fields[11]:-0}"
  stime="${fields[12]:-0}"
  local fds=0 entries
  entries=(/proc/"$pid"/fd/*)
  if [ -e "${entries[0]}" ]; then fds="${#entries[@]}"; fi
  local cpu
  cpu="$(awk -v u="$utime" -v s="$stime" -v t="$PERF_CLK_TCK" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", (u+s)/t}')"
  printf '%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s,%s\n' \
    "$(perf_now_ns)" "$rss" "$hwm" "$thr" "$fds" "$utime" "$stime" "$cpu" "$label"
}

# perf_sampler_start <pid> <csv> [interval-s] [label]
perf_sampler_start() {
  local pid="$1" csv="$2" interval="${3:-0.5}" label="${4:-}"
  echo "$PERF_SAMPLE_HEADER" > "$csv"
  (
    while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
      perf_sample_row "$pid" "$label" >> "$csv" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep "$interval"
    done
  ) &
  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=$!
}

perf_sampler_stop() {
  [ -n "${PERF_SAMPLER_PID:-}" ] || return 0
  kill "$PERF_SAMPLER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$PERF_SAMPLER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=""
  return 0
}

# perf_sample_stats <csv> — "peak_rss_kb peak_hwm_kb max_fds max_threads
# last_cpu_sec first_rss_kb last_rss_kb samples" from a sampler CSV.
perf_sample_stats() {
  python3 - "$1" <<'PY'
import csv, sys
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(sys.argv[1])))
rows = [r for r in rows if r.get("rss_kb")]
if not rows:
    print("0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0"); raise SystemExit
i = lambda r, k: int(r[k] or 0)
print(max(i(r, "rss_kb") for r in rows),
      max(i(r, "hwm_kb") for r in rows),
      max(i(r, "fds") for r in rows),
      max(i(r, "threads") for r in rows),
      rows[-1]["cpu_sec"],
      i(rows[0], "rss_kb"),
      i(rows[-1], "rss_kb"),
      len(rows))
PY
}

# perf_proc_rss <pid> — VmRSS in kB, or 0.
perf_proc_rss() {
  local line
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in VmRSS:*) echo "${line//[!0-9]/}"; return 0 ;; esac
  done < "/proc/$1/status" 2>/dev/null
  echo 0
}
perf_proc_hwm() {
  local line
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in VmHWM:*) echo "${line//[!0-9]/}"; return 0 ;; esac
  done < "/proc/$1/status" 2>/dev/null
  echo 0
}
perf_proc_cpu_sec() {
  local stat rest fields
  stat="$(< "/proc/$1/stat")" 2>/dev/null || { echo 0; return 0; }
  rest="${stat#*') '}"
  read -ra fields <<< "$rest"
  awk -v u="${fields[11]:-0}" -v s="${fields[12]:-0}" -v t="$PERF_CLK_TCK" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", (u+s)/t}'
}
perf_proc_fds() {
  local entries
  entries=(/proc/"$1"/fd/*)
  if [ -e "${entries[0]}" ]; then echo "${#entries[@]}"; else echo 0; fi
}

# --- API driving -----------------------------------------------------------

PERF_ULID_ALPHABET=0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ

# A syntactically valid ULID (26 Crockford base32 chars, first char <= '7' so
# the 48-bit timestamp cannot overflow). The daemon only validates the shape.
perf_ulid() {
  local out="${PERF_ULID_ALPHABET:$((RANDOM % 8)):1}" i
  for ((i = 0; i < 25; i++)); do out+="${PERF_ULID_ALPHABET:$((RANDOM % 32)):1}"; done
  printf '%s' "$out"
}

perf_api() { # perf_api <method> <path> [json-body]
  local method="$1" path="$2" body="${3:-}"
  if [ -n "$body" ]; then
    curl -sS -m "${PERF_HTTP_TIMEOUT:-300}" -X "$method" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERF_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d "$body" "$PERF_ENDPOINT$path"
  else
    curl -sS -m "${PERF_HTTP_TIMEOUT:-300}" -X "$method" \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERF_TOKEN" "$PERF_ENDPOINT$path"
  fi
}

# perf_timed_get <path> <outfile> — GET timed with curl's own clock.
# Prints "wall_ns http_code bytes curl_total_s".
perf_timed_get() {
  local path="$1" out="${2:-/dev/null}" t0 t1 line
  perf_mark t0
  line="$(curl -sS -m "${PERF_HTTP_TIMEOUT:-300}" -o "$out" \
    -w '%{http_code} %{size_download} %{time_total}' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $PERF_TOKEN" "$PERF_ENDPOINT$path" 2>/dev/null)"
  perf_mark t1
  printf '%s %s\n' "$((t1 - t0))" "$line"
}

# perf_submit <intent> [cwd] [backend] — one synchronous submit; prints the
# work id (empty on failure). Body is built before the clock starts.
perf_submit() {
  local intent="$1" cwd="${2:-${PERF_REPO:-}}" backend="${3:-fake}" body resp
  body="$(jq -nc --arg cid "$(perf_ulid)" --arg intent "$intent" --arg cwd "$cwd" --arg b "$backend" \
    '{command_id:$cid, intent:$intent, backend:$b, origin:{client:"cli", cwd:$cwd}}')"
  resp="$(perf_api POST /v1/work "$body")"
  jq -r '.work.id // empty' <<< "$resp"
}

# perf_respond <work-id> <input> — prints the resulting work state.
perf_respond() {
  local id="$1" input="$2" body resp
  body="$(jq -nc --arg cid "$(perf_ulid)" --arg i "$input" '{command_id:$cid, input:$i}')"
  resp="$(perf_api POST "/v1/work/$id/input" "$body")"
  jq -r '.work.state // .error.code // "?"' <<< "$resp"
}

perf_cancel() {
  local id="$1" body
  body="$(jq -nc --arg cid "$(perf_ulid)" '{command_id:$cid}')"
  perf_api POST "/v1/work/$id/cancel" "$body" > /dev/null
}

perf_work_state() { perf_api GET "/v1/work/$1" | jq -r '.work.state // "?"'; }

perf_journal_head() { perf_api GET /v1/system | jq -r '.journal_head // 0'; }

perf_state_counts() { # "state:count" lines over the whole fleet
  perf_api GET /v1/work | jq -r '[.works[].state] | group_by(.) | map({(.[0]): length}) | add // {} | to_entries[] | "\(.key):\(.value)"'
}

perf_count_state() { perf_api GET /v1/work | jq --arg s "$1" '[.works[] | select(.state == $s)] | length'; }

perf_journal_events() { # events on disk, independent of the daemon
  local dd="${1:-$PERF_DATA_DIR}"
  cat "$dd"/journal/*.ndjson 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# perf_burst <n> <parallel> <calls-dir> [intent-prefix]
#
# n concurrent submits through the HTTP API (one curl per call, xargs -P for
# fan-out) writing one CSV line per call into <calls-dir>. The submit path
# runs the whole workflow inside the request with the fake backend, so a call's
# latency is a work's end-to-end latency.
perf_burst() {
  local n="$1" par="$2" dir="$3" prefix="${4:-perf}"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  seq 1 "$n" | xargs -P "$par" -I@ \
    "$PERF_DIR/_submit-one.sh" "$PERF_ENDPOINT" "$PERF_TOKEN" "${PERF_REPO:-}" "$prefix-@" "$dir/@.csv"
}

# perf_collect_calls <calls-dir> <out-csv> — concatenate per-call CSVs.
perf_collect_calls() {
  local dir="$1" out="$2"
  echo 't_start_ns,wall_ns,curl_total_s,http_code,work_id,state' > "$out"
  cat "$dir"/*.csv 2>/dev/null >> "$out" || true
}

# --- statistics ------------------------------------------------------------

# perf_pctl — numbers on stdin, prints "count min p50 p95 p99 max mean".
#
# `python3 -c`, not a heredoc: a heredoc *is* python's stdin, which would eat
# the numbers being piped in (this cost one silent run of all-zero latency
# columns before it was caught).
perf_pctl() {
  python3 -c '
import sys
xs = sorted(float(x) for x in sys.stdin.read().split() if x.strip())
if not xs:
    print("0 0 0 0 0 0 0"); raise SystemExit
def p(q):
    if len(xs) == 1: return xs[0]
    k = q * (len(xs) - 1)
    lo, hi = int(k), min(int(k) + 1, len(xs) - 1)
    return xs[lo] + (xs[hi] - xs[lo]) * (k - lo)
print(len(xs), "%.3f" % xs[0], "%.3f" % p(.5), "%.3f" % p(.95), "%.3f" % p(.99),
      "%.3f" % xs[-1], "%.3f" % (sum(xs) / len(xs)))
'
}

perf_ms() { awk -v n="$1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", n/1000000}'; }
perf_s()  { awk -v n="$1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", n/1000000000}'; }

# perf_latency_kv <prefix> <csv> <column-index-1based>
# Emits <prefix>_{count,min_ms,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,max_ms,mean_ms} from a
# calls CSV whose column holds nanoseconds.
perf_latency_kv() {
  local prefix="$1" csv="$2" col="${3:-2}" stats
  stats="$(tail -n +2 "$csv" | cut -d, -f"$col" | grep -E '^[0-9]+$' | awk '{printf "%.3f\n", $1/1000000}' | perf_pctl)"
  read -r c mn p50 p95 p99 mx mean <<< "$stats"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_count" "$c"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_min_ms" "$mn"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_p50_ms" "$p50"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_p95_ms" "$p95"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_p99_ms" "$p99"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_max_ms" "$mx"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_mean_ms" "$mean"
}

# --- disk accounting -------------------------------------------------------

perf_bytes() { du -sb "$1" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1 || echo 0; }

perf_disk_kv() { # perf_disk_kv <prefix> <data-dir>
  local prefix="$1" dd="$2"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_total_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd")"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_journal_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd/journal")"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_blobs_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd/blobs")"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_surfaces_bytes" "$(perf_bytes "$dd/surfaces")"
  perf_kv "${prefix}_duckdb_bytes" "$(stat -c %s "$dd/projections/sergeant.duckdb" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
}

# --- hygiene sweep ---------------------------------------------------------

# perf_sgt_processes — sgt processes visible right now, one per line, with this
# harness's own shell and pgrep invocations filtered out. Never fails: pgrep
# and grep both exit 1 on "no matches", which under `set -o pipefail` would
# otherwise abort the caller.
perf_sgt_processes() {
  { pgrep -fa "release/sgt" 2>/dev/null; pgrep -fa "debug/sgt" 2>/dev/null; } \
    | grep -v "bash -c" | grep -v "scripts/perf" | grep -v "pgrep" || true
}

perf_sgt_process_count() {
  local list; list="$(perf_sgt_processes)"
  if [ -z "$list" ]; then echo 0; else printf '%s\n' "$list" | wc -l | tr -d ' '; fi
}


# perf_hygiene <label> [repo...] — the sweep P1-PERF ends every scenario with.
# Writes hygiene-<label>.txt and prints the verdict. Never exits nonzero: a
# dirty sweep is data the scenario must report, not a reason to abort.
perf_hygiene() {
  local label="$1"; shift
  local file="${PERF_OUT:-.}/hygiene-${label}.txt"
  local orphans strays worktrees=0 repo verdict=clean
  # Repos may arrive both as arguments and in PERF_REPOS; count each once.
  local repos=() seen existing
  for repo in "$@" "${PERF_REPOS[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$repo" ] && [ -d "$repo/.git" ] || continue
    seen=no
    for existing in "${repos[@]:-}"; do [ "$existing" = "$repo" ] && seen=yes; done
    [ "$seen" = no ] && repos+=("$repo")
  done
  # pgrep's own invocation is wrapped in a `bash -c` whose command line holds
  # the pattern; that self-match is filtered, nothing else is.
  orphans="$(perf_sgt_processes)"
  strays="$(ls -d /tmp/.tmp* /tmp/sgt-demo-* "/tmp/tmux-$(id -u)"/sgtperf-* 2>/dev/null || true)"
  {
    echo "hygiene sweep: $label   ($(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ))"
    echo "-- sgt processes"
    if [ -n "$orphans" ]; then echo "$orphans"; else echo "(none)"; fi
    echo "-- /tmp residue (.tmp*, sgt-demo-*, stale sgtperf tmux sockets)"
    if [ -n "$strays" ]; then echo "$strays"; else echo "(none)"; fi
    echo "-- worktrees"
    echo "   (a worktree under <data-dir>/surfaces/<work-id>/ belongs to that"
    echo "    work and is expected while the work is non-terminal: teardown"
    echo "    retires a surface only when the work reaches a terminal state.)"
    for repo in "${repos[@]:-}"; do
      echo "[$repo]"
      git -C "$repo" worktree list 2>/dev/null || true
    done
    echo "-- surfaces dirs"
    if [ -n "${PERF_DATA_DIR:-}" ] && [ -d "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" ]; then
      find "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 2>/dev/null || true
    else
      echo "(no surfaces dir)"
    fi
  } > "$file"
  local n
  for repo in "${repos[@]:-}"; do
    n="$(git -C "$repo" worktree list 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
    worktrees=$((worktrees + n))
  done
  local nproc_left=0
  [ -n "$orphans" ] && nproc_left="$(printf '%s\n' "$orphans" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  # Surfaces are counted in two buckets, because they mean different things:
  # a *populated* surface dir is a worktree that outlived its work (dirty), an
  # *empty* one is a directory teardown did not remove. Measured separately so
  # the second is reportable as its own finding instead of being lost inside a
  # "dirty" verdict.
  local nsurf=0 nsurf_nonempty=0 d
  if [ -n "${PERF_DATA_DIR:-}" ] && [ -d "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r d; do
      [ -n "$d" ] || continue
      nsurf=$((nsurf + 1))
      [ -n "$(ls -A "$d" 2>/dev/null)" ] && nsurf_nonempty=$((nsurf_nonempty + 1))
    done < <(find "$PERF_DATA_DIR/surfaces" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d 2>/dev/null)
  fi
  [ "$nproc_left" -eq 0 ] && [ "$worktrees" -eq 0 ] && [ "$nsurf_nonempty" -eq 0 ] || verdict=dirty
  perf_say "hygiene[$label]: $verdict — sgt procs=$nproc_left stray worktrees=$worktrees populated surfaces=$nsurf_nonempty empty surface dirs=$((nsurf - nsurf_nonempty)) (detail: $file)"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_verdict" "$verdict"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_sgt_processes" "$nproc_left"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_worktrees" "$worktrees"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs" "$nsurf"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs_populated" "$nsurf_nonempty"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs_empty_leftover" "$((nsurf - nsurf_nonempty))"
  local nstray=0
  [ -n "$strays" ] && nstray="$(printf '%s\n' "$strays" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_tmp_residue" "$nstray"
  return 0
}

# --- environment record ----------------------------------------------------

perf_environment() { # perf_environment <outfile>
  local out="$1"
  {
    echo "commit: ${PERF_COMMIT:-unknown}"
    echo "binary: $SGT_BIN"
    echo "sgt --version: $("$SGT_BIN" --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
    echo "nproc: $(nproc)"
    echo "cgroup cpu.max: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max 2>/dev/null || echo 'absent (cgroup v1)')"
    echo "cgroup v1 cfs_quota_us: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"
    echo "cgroup v1 cfs_period_us: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"
    echo "MemTotal: $(awk '/MemTotal/{print $2" kB"}' /proc/meminfo)"
    echo "kernel: $(uname -sr)"
    echo "CLK_TCK: $PERF_CLK_TCK"
    echo "df (output mount):"
    df -h "${PERF_OUT:-.}" | sed 's/^/  /'
    echo "ulimit -n: $(ulimit -n)"
  } | tee "$out"
}
