1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Commands
6	
7	```sh
8	cargo build                                          # debug build of the `sgt` binary
9	cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test
10	                                                     # the gates; all three must be green before any commit
11	cargo test --test m4_backends                        # one suite (m1_event_core … m6_surfaces)
12	cargo test --test m6_surfaces t5                     # one test by name substring
13	SERGEANT_CLAUDE_TESTS=1 cargo test --test m4_backends -- --ignored
14	                                                     # opt-in tests against the real `claude` CLI (bills tokens)
15	scripts/demo.sh                                      # §39 end-to-end walkthrough, fake backend, exits 0 or the walkthrough is broken
16	scripts/gate.sh "<intent>"                           # shipping gate via the no-mistakes pipeline (see below)
17	```
18	
19	First build is slow: bundled DuckDB compiles ~500 C++ translation units (~10 min cold). `Cargo.toml` pins `[profile.dev.package.libduckdb-sys] debug = false` — removing it balloons `target/` from ~5 GB to ~15 GB. Never point an external pipeline's builds at this checkout's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`: shared caches bake foreign `env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR)` paths into reused test binaries (diagnosed 2026-08-09, see the ledger's M6 pause marker). The same hazard's other face: a disposable probe copy that shares this checkout's cache overwrites its binary slots — after any probe-copy build, rebuild the main checkout before measuring `target/debug/sgt` (bit twice, 2026-08-10, Bug Sprint 1 entry).
20	
21	## What this is
22	
23	A local agent execution daemon (`sgt`): durable Work items run staged workflows in git-worktree surfaces, executed by native agent harnesses (Claude via headless `claude -p` turns; a deterministic fake backend for tests), with the entire trajectory event-sourced into an append-only journal. Specified by `reference/proposal-depot-rust-execution-surface.md` (which calls the product "Depot"); the N-series (ICM workflows, per-stage harnesses, Docker execute stages) is governed by its successor, `reference/proposal-next-iteration-icm-workflows.md`, kicked off by the N0 contract's rulings. Departures from either proposal live in GAUNTLET.md's deviation register and are settled — re-litigate one only by arguing its ruling is wrong, not by noticing the deviation exists.
24	
25	## Architecture — the invariants that shape everything
26	
27	- **The journal is the only truth.** Every state change is an event appended to a segmented, crash-tolerant JSONL journal (`src/runtime/journal.rs`; large payloads in a BLAKE3 content-addressed blob store). Everything else — the in-memory work projection, the DuckDB analytics tables (`src/runtime/analytics.rs`), the graph projection, every client screen — is a disposable projection rebuilt from it. Rebuild-on-start is the only population path; there is no snapshot loading (backlog B1 explains why).
28	- **One owner.** The daemon (`src/daemon.rs`) exclusively owns the data dir (daemon.lock) and all process handles. Clients hold no state and never touch storage.
29	- **Clients are equal.** The CLI, TUI (`src/tui.rs`), and embedded dashboard (`src/web.rs`) reach state only through the loopback HTTP/SSE API (`src/api.rs`) via `ApiClient`/`ApiViews`. This is enforced by tests, not convention: `tests/m6_surfaces.rs` t5 scans for internals imports AND pins the exact public method set of `ApiViews` — widening that surface with a non-endpoint method fails the test by design. If a client needs something the API lacks, extend the API.
30	- **Work state ≠ process state.** A Claude "session" is a durable conversation identity; the OS process exists per turn. Restart reconciliation (`src/runtime/recovery.rs`) resumes only on unambiguous evidence; ambiguity fails closed into `blocked` with a reason, never a guess.
31	- **Adjacent-append crash windows** are this architecture's recurring hazard (LESSONS L6): any path appending two causally-linked events must tolerate the second one missing or write one compound event. Check for this class in review of any journal-touching change.
32	
33	Layout: single crate, lib + thin `main.rs` (`src/lib.rs` declares modules; integration tests need the lib target). `src/domain/` = types, `src/runtime/` = journal/projections/engine/recovery/router/analytics/graph, `src/backend/` = the §15 `Backend` trait + claude/fake (codex is a doc-stub per D6), `src/{api,cli,tui,web,daemon,telemetry}.rs` = surfaces.
34	
35	## Testing rules specific to this repo
36	
37	- Tests live in per-milestone suites `tests/m1_event_core.rs` … `tests/m6_surfaces.rs` (379 total + 4 opt-in as of the invariants/test-honesty round-2 fixer, 2026-08-11 — coverage 94.63% lines measured at S2 close by the committed convention, `docs/coverage/baseline-2026-08-10.md`; the count is a smoke check on this line, not a budget, and TH-R2-03 confirmed round 1's TH-9 fix here had already gone stale again by the very next diff — re-measure with `cargo test` rather than trusting this line). Suites that spawn daemons MUST go through `tests/support/mod.rs`'s `DataDir` guard — the `sgt(...)` helpers take `&DataDir` so an unreaped auto-spawned daemon is a type error, and the guard reaps by `/proc` argv scan on Drop. This exists because a measured leak accumulated ~89 orphan daemons in a day.
38	- A fix without a test that fails when the fix is reverted is not done (LESSONS L7). Every advertised backend capability flag needs a contract test against the installed harness (L8).
39	- The Claude adapter's behavior is *measured*, never assumed from docs — exit codes lie, `subtype` lies, model aliases silently substitute (L1). The version gate is pinned in `src/backend/claude.rs`; re-measure on any CLI version bump.
40	- **Code is code (R-S0-12).** Any diff that changes executable behavior — `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, CI config, workflow `.js` — takes the full multi-axis loop (panel, adversarial verify, fix, adjudication). Measurement-template exemptions cover only phases that write no code; a builder's self-probe is panel input, never a substitute (L13).
41	- Tests run in two known environments with opposite constraints — design fault-injection fixtures for both or probe-gate with a loud `SKIPPED-ENV`: the root dev container (permission-bit tricks silently pass; EAGAIN≡EWOULDBLOCK; O_APPEND defeats post-start file sabotage) and GitHub's non-root 2-core runner (no `CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE`; O_DIRECT alignment unenforced). Locally-fixable preconditions stay hard failures; shapes no hosted-runner user can change skip loudly (GAUNTLET.md's S2 entry, issue #31 / Environmental behavior, has the run evidence).
42	- After running suites, `pgrep -f "debug/sgt [-]-data-dir"` should find nothing — that bracket is the whole trick: it makes the checking command non-self-matching (an unbracketed pattern matches your own shell; this bit two sessions).
43	- Commits that fully close an issue carry a `Fixes #NN` trailer; a PR body lists only closures whose commits are actually on the branch (Bug Sprint 1 / S2 precedent).
44	
45	## The development record (read before changing method or scope)
46	
47	- **GAUNTLET.md** — append-only ledger: the deviation register, backlog rows with named triggers, per-milestone scorecards and adjudication rulings (current numbering lives in the file itself, not here — refer, don't copy). Append; never rewrite history.
48	- **LESSONS.md** — binding on development here. Highest-leverage: measure the claude CLI (L1), point fresh reviewers at the register first (L3), mutation probes only in disposable copies outside the tree (L5), keep fix commits separable from build commits (L10), re-read governing text at decision time — summaries are orientation, not authority (L12).
49	- **docs/gauntlet/contracts/** — the milestone contracts the code was built and reviewed against; `reference/notes/gauntlet-pattern.md` defines the loop **and the binding model spread** (Sonnet executes contracts, Opus judges outcomes, Fable is the one orchestrator seat and never fans out — dated revision 2026-08-10, ruling R-S0-13); `resources/` holds every orchestration script as run, per-series.
50	- Design decisions log their Ponytail rung (R1–R7 ladder in `reference/notes/ideaos-agent-contract.md`).
51	- `reference/notes/` are **living method docs**, revised in place with dated entries (their own convention — see the economy revisions). Everything else under `reference/` — the proposals, `sergeant-upstream/` — is frozen evidence: don't edit it to change behavior.
52	
53	## Shipping gate
54	
55	`scripts/gate.sh "<intent>"` runs the no-mistakes pipeline (`--skip push,pr,ci`; push/PR handled manually). It requires a clean tree, self-heals the pipeline daemon with the env the host needs (`IS_SANDBOX=1` only under root — it exists for root containers; the script is portable across the measured `docs/environments/` hosts), and gives the pipeline a private cargo cache. While a run is active the branch is pipeline-owned: don't commit locally until the run reaches an outcome, then `no-mistakes axi respond` on gates and `no-mistakes axi sync --recover` to take custody of pipeline commits.
56	
57	Remote containers do not ship with no-mistakes — install it at session start. The release installer (`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes/main/docs/install.sh | sh`) 403s through this environment's proxy (release-API fetches are blocked); the working path is source build, the M1 precedent: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes && go build -o ~/.cargo/bin/no-mistakes ./cmd/no-mistakes` (Go is preinstalled). Note the built version in the ledger entry that first uses it (M-series pinned v1.47.0; drift is a fact to record, not a blocker). If the gate genuinely cannot run, the fallback regime is R-S0-1 (orchestrator-verified gates + hygiene sweep), recorded per milestone — never silence.
58	
59	## Environments
60	
61	Repo invariants live in this file; **per-host facts live in `docs/environments/`** (one dated, evidence-cited file per environment — cloud container, GH runner, and each new host on first contact). Never assume another environment's facts apply: measure, then record there. Fixtures asserting environment facts probe-gate per the testing rules above.
62	
63	Run `scripts/probe-env.sh` once at session start on **any** host, before doing anything else — it measures uid/DAC/CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE, disk and writable-allowance, O_DIRECT alignment behavior (open AND unaligned-write, the two-valued fact the journal's fault-injection fixtures actually branch on), network/proxy posture, Docker, and the claude/cargo/rustc toolchain, and prints them as a dated markdown table in the exact `docs/environments/` format — paste its output into that host's file. It never exits nonzero for an absent tool or negative result (only for its own bug); regression coverage lives in `scripts/probe-env-selftest.sh`, run with `bash scripts/probe-env-selftest.sh`.
64	
65	## Remote-container operations
66	
67	These sessions run in ephemeral containers that reset without warning (three resets in one S-series day; a reset also wipes installed tools and `target/`, costing a ~10-min cold DuckDB rebuild):
68	
69	- **Push after every green gate.** Anything unpushed can vanish; everything pushed made the S2 resets free. In-flight workflows survive via cache-resume (`resumeFromRunId`) — orphaned agents' commits recover from git.
70	- **On wake or after any reset, restore before touching anything**: `git fetch origin <branch> && git checkout <branch> && git reset --hard origin/<branch>`. A freshly reset container silently gives you a stale clone of `main`; two S-session near-misses started by editing it.
71	- Re-install no-mistakes (above) and re-warm the build in the background while doing doc work.
72

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# P1-PERF — the whole matrix, in order, one command.
#
#   scripts/perf/run-all.sh <outdir>
#
# Records the environment, takes the idle-daemon baseline, then runs S1..S7
# strictly sequentially — never overlapping another scenario's measurement
# window, each into its own subdirectory of <outdir>, each against its own
# fresh data dir. A scenario that fails is recorded as failed and the run
# continues: "a scenario that cannot hit its target records where it stopped
# and why — that is data, not failure."
#
# Every scenario is also runnable alone: scripts/perf/s3-deep.sh <outdir>.
#
# Knobs: PERF_ONLY ("s1 s4" to run a subset), PERF_SKIP_IDLE=1.
# Scenario-level knobs are documented in each scenario's header and pass
# through this script unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=common.sh
. "$HERE/common.sh"

OUT="${1:?usage: run-all.sh <outdir>}"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
OUT="$(cd "$OUT" && pwd)"
perf_require_binary

LOG="$OUT/run-all.log"
STATUS="$OUT/run-all-status.tsv"
: > "$STATUS"

{
  echo "P1-PERF full run"
  echo "started: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
  echo "outdir:  $OUT"
  echo
  PERF_OUT="$OUT" perf_environment "$OUT/environment.txt"
} | tee "$LOG"

ONLY="${PERF_ONLY:-}"
wanted() {
  [ -z "$ONLY" ] && return 0
  case " $ONLY " in *" $1 "*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}

run_stage() { # run_stage <name> <script> <subdir>
  local name="$1" script="$2" sub="$3"
  wanted "$name" || { printf '%s\tskipped\t0\n' "$name" >> "$STATUS"; return 0; }
  printf '\n\033[1m######## %s ########\033[0m\n' "$name" | tee -a "$LOG"
  local t0 t1 rc
  perf_mark t0
  "$script" "$OUT/$sub" 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG"
  rc="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
  perf_mark t1
  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$name" "$([ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && echo ok || echo "failed(rc=$rc)")" "$(perf_s $((t1 - t0)))" >> "$STATUS"
  # Between scenarios: nothing of this one may still be running.
  sleep 3
}

if [ "${PERF_SKIP_IDLE:-0}" != 1 ]; then
  run_stage idle "$HERE/idle-baseline.sh" idle
fi
run_stage s1 "$HERE/s1-burst.sh"   s1
run_stage s2 "$HERE/s2-churn.sh"   s2
run_stage s3 "$HERE/s3-deep.sh"    s3
run_stage s4 "$HERE/s4-sse.sh"     s4
run_stage s5 "$HERE/s5-journal.sh" s5
run_stage s6 "$HERE/s6-crash.sh"   s6
run_stage s7 "$HERE/s7-clients.sh" s7

printf '\n\033[1m######## run complete ########\033[0m\n' | tee -a "$LOG"
{
  printf '%-8s %-16s %s\n' scenario outcome wall_s
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r name outcome wall; do
    printf '%-8s %-16s %s\n' "$name" "$outcome" "$wall"
  done < "$STATUS"
} | tee -a "$LOG"

# Final sweep across everything the run created.
---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Idle daemon baseline — recorded before any scenario (P1-PERF measurement rule
# 3): a freshly started daemon on an empty data dir, doing nothing, sampled for
# two minutes. RSS, fds and CPU over that window are the floor every other
# number in the baseline is read against.
#
#   scripts/perf/idle-baseline.sh <outdir>
#
# Knobs: PERF_IDLE_SECS (120), PERF_IDLE_INTERVAL (1).
set -euo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=common.sh
. "$HERE/common.sh"

OUT="${1:?usage: idle-baseline.sh <outdir>}"
perf_init "$OUT" idle-baseline

SECS="${PERF_IDLE_SECS:-120}"
INTERVAL="${PERF_IDLE_INTERVAL:-1}"

perf_environment "$PERF_OUT/environment.txt" > /dev/null

DD="$PERF_SCRATCH/idle/data"
rm -rf "$PERF_SCRATCH/idle"
mkdir -p "$DD"
perf_daemon_start "$DD"
perf_say "daemon pid $PERF_DAEMON_PID · sampling ${SECS}s at ${INTERVAL}s"
perf_kv settle_s "$SECS"
perf_kv sample_interval_s "$INTERVAL"
perf_kv cold_start_empty_ms "$PERF_DAEMON_READY_MS"

CSV="$PERF_OUT/idle-sample.csv"
cpu0="$(perf_proc_cpu_sec "$PERF_DAEMON_PID")"
perf_sampler_start "$PERF_DAEMON_PID" "$CSV" "$INTERVAL" idle
sleep "$SECS"
perf_sampler_stop
cpu1="$(perf_proc_cpu_sec "$PERF_DAEMON_PID")"

read -r peak_rss peak_hwm max_fds max_thr last_cpu first_rss last_rss nsamples <<< "$(perf_sample_stats "$CSV")"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/perf/common.sh — shared helpers for the P1-PERF load/stress harness.
#
# Sourced by every s*-*.sh scenario and by run-all.sh. Nothing here measures
# anything on its own; it supplies the four things every scenario needs:
#
#   * a scenario workspace   — fresh data dir + a seeded git repo (demo.sh's
#                              recipe: .sergeant/workflows/<name>/<stage>/)
#   * a daemon under control — spawned with a chosen SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT, its pid
#                              read from the runtime descriptor (the documented
#                              client handshake), stopped and verified stopped
#   * /proc sampling         — VmRSS / VmHWM / threads / fd count / utime+stime
#                              into CSV, either one row on demand or a
#                              background sampler at a chosen interval
#   * measurement plumbing   — latency timing, percentiles, a summary block
#                              that is printed and written as JSON, and the
#                              hygiene sweep
#
# The harness drives the shipped release binary and its loopback HTTP API and
# adds no Rust (P1-PERF non-goal: "new Rust code beyond what a scenario
# strictly needs"). High-rate cells drive POST /v1/... with curl rather than
# one CLI process per call, because the CLI spawns a process per call and that
# is the client's cost, not the daemon's.
#
# Nothing under here writes into the repository tree: every scenario's data
# dirs, repos and raw output live under the <outdir> it is given.

# --- resolution ------------------------------------------------------------

PERF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PERF_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$PERF_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# The unit under test is the release build (P1-PERF: "the baseline describes
# what ships, not debug-profile DuckDB").
SGT_BIN="${SGT_BIN:-$PERF_REPO_ROOT/target/release/sgt}"

PERF_CLK_TCK="$(getconf CLK_TCK 2>/dev/null || echo 100)"

# Timing: CLOCK_REALTIME nanoseconds. `date +%s%N` costs a fork (~2 ms on this
# container) which is the same order as the thing being measured, so the
# fork-free bash-5 EPOCHREALTIME is preferred and `date` is the fallback. Same
# clock, same units.
perf_now_ns() {
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    printf '%s%s\n' "$sec" "${frac:0:9}"
  else
    date +%s%N
  fi
}

# perf_mark VAR — assign "now" in ns to VAR without forking a subshell.
perf_mark() {
  local -n __perf_mark_out=$1
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    __perf_mark_out="${sec}${frac:0:9}"
  else
    __perf_mark_out="$(date +%s%N)"
  fi
}

perf_die() { printf '\033[31mperf: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
perf_say() { printf '   %s\n' "$*"; }
perf_step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
perf_warn() { printf '\033[33m   ! %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; }

perf_require_binary() {
  [ -x "$SGT_BIN" ] || perf_die "no release binary at $SGT_BIN (cargo build --release)"
  for tool in curl jq python3 git; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || perf_die "missing required tool: $tool"
  done
  # The tested binary's identity, captured exactly once — a live rev-parse per
  # scenario tracks the checkout, not the binary: a commit landing mid-matrix
  # made 6 of 8 scenarios self-report code that was never in the binary
  # (issue #50). Exported so scenarios spawned by run-all.sh inherit the pin
  # instead of re-reading HEAD.
  if [ -z "${PERF_COMMIT:-}" ]; then
    PERF_COMMIT="$(git -C "$PERF_REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    export PERF_COMMIT
  fi
}

# --- scenario lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------

# perf_init <outdir> <scenario-name>
#
# Creates the output dir, the scenario's scratch dir (data dirs and seed repos
# live there, never in the repo tree), opens the summary accumulator, and
# installs the teardown trap so an aborted scenario still stops its daemon.
perf_init() {
  PERF_OUT="$1"
  PERF_SCENARIO="$2"
  perf_require_binary
  mkdir -p "$PERF_OUT"
  PERF_OUT="$(cd "$PERF_OUT" && pwd)"
  PERF_SCRATCH="$PERF_OUT/scratch"
  mkdir -p "$PERF_SCRATCH"
  PERF_SUMMARY_TSV="$PERF_OUT/${PERF_SCENARIO}-summary.tsv"
  : > "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV"
  PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=""
  PERF_FORCE_KILLED=0
  PERF_REPOS=()
  PERF_START_NS="$(perf_now_ns)"
  trap 'perf_teardown' EXIT
  perf_step "$PERF_SCENARIO — output $PERF_OUT"
  perf_kv scenario "$PERF_SCENARIO"
  perf_kv binary "$SGT_BIN"
  perf_kv commit "$PERF_COMMIT"
  perf_kv started_at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
}

perf_teardown() {
  local rc=$?
  perf_sampler_stop >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if [ -n "${PERF_DAEMON_PID:-}" ] && kill -0 "$PERF_DAEMON_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
    perf_daemon_stop "$PERF_DAEMON_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  return $rc
}

# --- the summary block -----------------------------------------------------

# perf_kv <key> <value> — one distilled measurement.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/perf/common.sh — shared helpers for the P1-PERF load/stress harness.
#
# Sourced by every s*-*.sh scenario and by run-all.sh. Nothing here measures
# anything on its own; it supplies the four things every scenario needs:
#
#   * a scenario workspace   — fresh data dir + a seeded git repo (demo.sh's
#                              recipe: .sergeant/workflows/<name>/<stage>/)
#   * a daemon under control — spawned with a chosen SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT, its pid
#                              read from the runtime descriptor (the documented
#                              client handshake), stopped and verified stopped
#   * /proc sampling         — VmRSS / VmHWM / threads / fd count / utime+stime
#                              into CSV, either one row on demand or a
#                              background sampler at a chosen interval
#   * measurement plumbing   — latency timing, percentiles, a summary block
#                              that is printed and written as JSON, and the
#                              hygiene sweep
#
# The harness drives the shipped release binary and its loopback HTTP API and
# adds no Rust (P1-PERF non-goal: "new Rust code beyond what a scenario
# strictly needs"). High-rate cells drive POST /v1/... with curl rather than
# one CLI process per call, because the CLI spawns a process per call and that
# is the client's cost, not the daemon's.
#
# Nothing under here writes into the repository tree: every scenario's data
# dirs, repos and raw output live under the <outdir> it is given.

# --- resolution ------------------------------------------------------------

PERF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PERF_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$PERF_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# The unit under test is the release build (P1-PERF: "the baseline describes
# what ships, not debug-profile DuckDB").
SGT_BIN="${SGT_BIN:-$PERF_REPO_ROOT/target/release/sgt}"

PERF_CLK_TCK="$(getconf CLK_TCK 2>/dev/null || echo 100)"

# Timing: CLOCK_REALTIME nanoseconds. `date +%s%N` costs a fork (~2 ms on this
# container) which is the same order as the thing being measured, so the
# fork-free bash-5 EPOCHREALTIME is preferred and `date` is the fallback. Same
# clock, same units.
perf_now_ns() {
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    printf '%s%s\n' "$sec" "${frac:0:9}"
  else
    date +%s%N
  fi
}

# perf_mark VAR — assign "now" in ns to VAR without forking a subshell.
perf_mark() {
  local -n __perf_mark_out=$1
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    __perf_mark_out="${sec}${frac:0:9}"
  else
    __perf_mark_out="$(date +%s%N)"
  fi
}

perf_die() { printf '\033[31mperf: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
perf_say() { printf '   %s\n' "$*"; }
perf_step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
perf_warn() { printf '\033[33m   ! %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; }

perf_require_binary() {
  [ -x "$SGT_BIN" ] || perf_die "no release binary at $SGT_BIN (cargo build --release)"
  for tool in curl jq python3 git; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || perf_die "missing required tool: $tool"
  done
  # The tested binary's identity, captured exactly once — a live rev-parse per
  # scenario tracks the checkout, not the binary: a commit landing mid-matrix
  # made 6 of 8 scenarios self-report code that was never in the binary
  # (issue #50). Exported so scenarios spawned by run-all.sh inherit the pin
  # instead of re-reading HEAD.
  if [ -z "${PERF_COMMIT:-}" ]; then
    PERF_COMMIT="$(git -C "$PERF_REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    export PERF_COMMIT
  fi
}

# --- scenario lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------

# perf_init <outdir> <scenario-name>
#
# Creates the output dir, the scenario's scratch dir (data dirs and seed repos
# live there, never in the repo tree), opens the summary accumulator, and
# installs the teardown trap so an aborted scenario still stops its daemon.
perf_init() {
  PERF_OUT="$1"
  PERF_SCENARIO="$2"
  perf_require_binary
  mkdir -p "$PERF_OUT"
  PERF_OUT="$(cd "$PERF_OUT" && pwd)"
  PERF_SCRATCH="$PERF_OUT/scratch"
  mkdir -p "$PERF_SCRATCH"
  PERF_SUMMARY_TSV="$PERF_OUT/${PERF_SCENARIO}-summary.tsv"
  : > "$PERF_SUMMARY_TSV"
  PERF_DAEMON_PID=""
  PERF_SAMPLER_PID=""
  PERF_FORCE_KILLED=0
  PERF_REPOS=()
  PERF_START_NS="$(perf_now_ns)"
  trap 'perf_teardown' EXIT
  perf_step "$PERF_SCENARIO — output $PERF_OUT"
  perf_kv scenario "$PERF_SCENARIO"
  perf_kv binary "$SGT_BIN"
  perf_kv commit "$PERF_COMMIT"
  perf_kv started_at "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
}

perf_teardown() {
  local rc=$?
=== ENVIRON
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs" "$nsurf"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs_populated" "$nsurf_nonempty"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_surface_dirs_empty_leftover" "$((nsurf - nsurf_nonempty))"
  local nstray=0
  [ -n "$strays" ] && nstray="$(printf '%s\n' "$strays" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  perf_kv "hygiene_${label}_tmp_residue" "$nstray"
  return 0
}

# --- environment record ----------------------------------------------------

perf_environment() { # perf_environment <outfile>
  local out="$1"
  {
    echo "commit: ${PERF_COMMIT:-unknown}"
    echo "binary: $SGT_BIN"
    echo "sgt --version: $("$SGT_BIN" --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
    echo "nproc: $(nproc)"
    echo "cgroup cpu.max: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max 2>/dev/null || echo 'absent (cgroup v1)')"
    echo "cgroup v1 cfs_quota_us: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_quota_us 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"
    echo "cgroup v1 cfs_period_us: $(cat /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu/cpu.cfs_period_us 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"
    echo "MemTotal: $(awk '/MemTotal/{print $2" kB"}' /proc/meminfo)"
    echo "kernel: $(uname -sr)"
    echo "CLK_TCK: $PERF_CLK_TCK"
    echo "df (output mount):"
    df -h "${PERF_OUT:-.}" | sed 's/^/  /'
    echo "ulimit -n: $(ulimit -n)"
  } | tee "$out"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# P1-PERF — the whole matrix, in order, one command.
#
#   scripts/perf/run-all.sh <outdir>
#
# Records the environment, takes the idle-daemon baseline, then runs S1..S7
# strictly sequentially — never overlapping another scenario's measurement
# window, each into its own subdirectory of <outdir>, each against its own
# fresh data dir. A scenario that fails is recorded as failed and the run
# continues: "a scenario that cannot hit its target records where it stopped
# and why — that is data, not failure."
#
# Every scenario is also runnable alone: scripts/perf/s3-deep.sh <outdir>.
#
# Knobs: PERF_ONLY ("s1 s4" to run a subset), PERF_SKIP_IDLE=1.
# Scenario-level knobs are documented in each scenario's header and pass
# through this script unchanged.
set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=common.sh
. "$HERE/common.sh"

OUT="${1:?usage: run-all.sh <outdir>}"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
OUT="$(cd "$OUT" && pwd)"
perf_require_binary

LOG="$OUT/run-all.log"
STATUS="$OUT/run-all-status.tsv"
: > "$STATUS"

71 CLAUDE.md
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Commands

```sh
cargo build                                          # debug build of the `sgt` binary
cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test
                                                     # the gates; all three must be green before any commit
cargo test --test m4_backends                        # one suite (m1_event_core … m6_surfaces)
cargo test --test m6_surfaces t5                     # one test by name substring
SERGEANT_CLAUDE_TESTS=1 cargo test --test m4_backends -- --ignored
                                                     # opt-in tests against the real `claude` CLI (bills tokens)
scripts/demo.sh                                      # §39 end-to-end walkthrough, fake backend, exits 0 or the walkthrough is broken
scripts/gate.sh "<intent>"                           # shipping gate via the no-mistakes pipeline (see below)
```

First build is slow: bundled DuckDB compiles ~500 C++ translation units (~10 min cold). `Cargo.toml` pins `[profile.dev.package.libduckdb-sys] debug = false` — removing it balloons `target/` from ~5 GB to ~15 GB. Never point an external pipeline's builds at this checkout's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`: shared caches bake foreign `env!(CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR)` paths into reused test binaries (diagnosed 2026-08-09, see the ledger's M6 pause marker). The same hazard's other face: a disposable probe copy that shares this checkout's cache overwrites its binary slots — after any probe-copy build, rebuild the main checkout before measuring `target/debug/sgt` (bit twice, 2026-08-10, Bug Sprint 1 entry).

## What this is

A local agent execution daemon (`sgt`): durable Work items run staged workflows in git-worktree surfaces, executed by native agent harnesses (Claude via headless `claude -p` turns; a deterministic fake backend for tests), with the entire trajectory event-sourced into an append-only journal. Specified by `reference/proposal-depot-rust-execution-surface.md` (which calls the product "Depot"); the N-series (ICM workflows, per-stage harnesses, Docker execute stages) is governed by its successor, `reference/proposal-next-iteration-icm-workflows.md`, kicked off by the N0 contract's rulings. Departures from either proposal live in GAUNTLET.md's deviation register and are settled — re-litigate one only by arguing its ruling is wrong, not by noticing the deviation exists.

## Architecture — the invariants that shape everything

- **The journal is the only truth.** Every state change is an event appended to a segmented, crash-tolerant JSONL journal (`src/runtime/journal.rs`; large payloads in a BLAKE3 content-addressed blob store). Everything else — the in-memory work projection, the DuckDB analytics tables (`src/runtime/analytics.rs`), the graph projection, every client screen — is a disposable projection rebuilt from it. Rebuild-on-start is the only population path; there is no snapshot loading (backlog B1 explains why).
- **One owner.** The daemon (`src/daemon.rs`) exclusively owns the data dir (daemon.lock) and all process handles. Clients hold no state and never touch storage.
- **Clients are equal.** The CLI, TUI (`src/tui.rs`), and embedded dashboard (`src/web.rs`) reach state only through the loopback HTTP/SSE API (`src/api.rs`) via `ApiClient`/`ApiViews`. This is enforced by tests, not convention: `tests/m6_surfaces.rs` t5 scans for internals imports AND pins the exact public method set of `ApiViews` — widening that surface with a non-endpoint method fails the test by design. If a client needs something the API lacks, extend the API.
- **Work state ≠ process state.** A Claude "session" is a durable conversation identity; the OS process exists per turn. Restart reconciliation (`src/runtime/recovery.rs`) resumes only on unambiguous evidence; ambiguity fails closed into `blocked` with a reason, never a guess.
- **Adjacent-append crash windows** are this architecture's recurring hazard (LESSONS L6): any path appending two causally-linked events must tolerate the second one missing or write one compound event. Check for this class in review of any journal-touching change.

Layout: single crate, lib + thin `main.rs` (`src/lib.rs` declares modules; integration tests need the lib target). `src/domain/` = types, `src/runtime/` = journal/projections/engine/recovery/router/analytics/graph, `src/backend/` = the §15 `Backend` trait + claude/fake (codex is a doc-stub per D6), `src/{api,cli,tui,web,daemon,telemetry}.rs` = surfaces.

## Testing rules specific to this repo

- Tests live in per-milestone suites `tests/m1_event_core.rs` … `tests/m6_surfaces.rs` (379 total + 4 opt-in as of the invariants/test-honesty round-2 fixer, 2026-08-11 — coverage 94.63% lines measured at S2 close by the committed convention, `docs/coverage/baseline-2026-08-10.md`; the count is a smoke check on this line, not a budget, and TH-R2-03 confirmed round 1's TH-9 fix here had already gone stale again by the very next diff — re-measure with `cargo test` rather than trusting this line). Suites that spawn daemons MUST go through `tests/support/mod.rs`'s `DataDir` guard — the `sgt(...)` helpers take `&DataDir` so an unreaped auto-spawned daemon is a type error, and the guard reaps by `/proc` argv scan on Drop. This exists because a measured leak accumulated ~89 orphan daemons in a day.
- A fix without a test that fails when the fix is reverted is not done (LESSONS L7). Every advertised backend capability flag needs a contract test against the installed harness (L8).
- The Claude adapter's behavior is *measured*, never assumed from docs — exit codes lie, `subtype` lies, model aliases silently substitute (L1). The version gate is pinned in `src/backend/claude.rs`; re-measure on any CLI version bump.
- **Code is code (R-S0-12).** Any diff that changes executable behavior — `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, CI config, workflow `.js` — takes the full multi-axis loop (panel, adversarial verify, fix, adjudication). Measurement-template exemptions cover only phases that write no code; a builder's self-probe is panel input, never a substitute (L13).
- Tests run in two known environments with opposite constraints — design fault-injection fixtures for both or probe-gate with a loud `SKIPPED-ENV`: the root dev container (permission-bit tricks silently pass; EAGAIN≡EWOULDBLOCK; O_APPEND defeats post-start file sabotage) and GitHub's non-root 2-core runner (no `CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE`; O_DIRECT alignment unenforced). Locally-fixable preconditions stay hard failures; shapes no hosted-runner user can change skip loudly (GAUNTLET.md's S2 entry, issue #31 / Environmental behavior, has the run evidence).
- After running suites, `pgrep -f "debug/sgt [-]-data-dir"` should find nothing — that bracket is the whole trick: it makes the checking command non-self-matching (an unbracketed pattern matches your own shell; this bit two sessions).
- Commits that fully close an issue carry a `Fixes #NN` trailer; a PR body lists only closures whose commits are actually on the branch (Bug Sprint 1 / S2 precedent).

## The development record (read before changing method or scope)

- **GAUNTLET.md** — append-only ledger: the deviation register, backlog rows with named triggers, per-milestone scorecards and adjudication rulings (current numbering lives in the file itself, not here — refer, don't copy). Append; never rewrite history.
- **LESSONS.md** — binding on development here. Highest-leverage: measure the claude CLI (L1), point fresh reviewers at the register first (L3), mutation probes only in disposable copies outside the tree (L5), keep fix commits separable from build commits (L10), re-read governing text at decision time — summaries are orientation, not authority (L12).
- **docs/gauntlet/contracts/** — the milestone contracts the code was built and reviewed against; `reference/notes/gauntlet-pattern.md` defines the loop **and the binding model spread** (Sonnet executes contracts, Opus judges outcomes, Fable is the one orchestrator seat and never fans out — dated revision 2026-08-10, ruling R-S0-13); `resources/` holds every orchestration script as run, per-series.
- Design decisions log their Ponytail rung (R1–R7 ladder in `reference/notes/ideaos-agent-contract.md`).
- `reference/notes/` are **living method docs**, revised in place with dated entries (their own convention — see the economy revisions). Everything else under `reference/` — the proposals, `sergeant-upstream/` — is frozen evidence: don't edit it to change behavior.

## Shipping gate

`scripts/gate.sh "<intent>"` runs the no-mistakes pipeline (`--skip push,pr,ci`; push/PR handled manually). It requires a clean tree, self-heals the pipeline daemon with the env the host needs (`IS_SANDBOX=1` only under root — it exists for root containers; the script is portable across the measured `docs/environments/` hosts), and gives the pipeline a private cargo cache. While a run is active the branch is pipeline-owned: don't commit locally until the run reaches an outcome, then `no-mistakes axi respond` on gates and `no-mistakes axi sync --recover` to take custody of pipeline commits.

Remote containers do not ship with no-mistakes — install it at session start. The release installer (`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes/main/docs/install.sh | sh`) 403s through this environment's proxy (release-API fetches are blocked); the working path is source build, the M1 precedent: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes && go build -o ~/.cargo/bin/no-mistakes ./cmd/no-mistakes` (Go is preinstalled). Note the built version in the ledger entry that first uses it (M-series pinned v1.47.0; drift is a fact to record, not a blocker). If the gate genuinely cannot run, the fallback regime is R-S0-1 (orchestrator-verified gates + hygiene sweep), recorded per milestone — never silence.

## Environments

Repo invariants live in this file; **per-host facts live in `docs/environments/`** (one dated, evidence-cited file per environment — cloud container, GH runner, and each new host on first contact). Never assume another environment's facts apply: measure, then record there. Fixtures asserting environment facts probe-gate per the testing rules above.

Run `scripts/probe-env.sh` once at session start on **any** host, before doing anything else — it measures uid/DAC/CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE, disk and writable-allowance, O_DIRECT alignment behavior (open AND unaligned-write, the two-valued fact the journal's fault-injection fixtures actually branch on), network/proxy posture, Docker, and the claude/cargo/rustc toolchain, and prints them as a dated markdown table in the exact `docs/environments/` format — paste its output into that host's file. It never exits nonzero for an absent tool or negative result (only for its own bug); regression coverage lives in `scripts/probe-env-selftest.sh`, run with `bash scripts/probe-env-selftest.sh`.

## Remote-container operations

These sessions run in ephemeral containers that reset without warning (three resets in one S-series day; a reset also wipes installed tools and `target/`, costing a ~10-min cold DuckDB rebuild):

- **Push after every green gate.** Anything unpushed can vanish; everything pushed made the S2 resets free. In-flight workflows survive via cache-resume (`resumeFromRunId`) — orphaned agents' commits recover from git.
- **On wake or after any reset, restore before touching anything**: `git fetch origin <branch> && git checkout <branch> && git reset --hard origin/<branch>`. A freshly reset container silently gives you a stale clone of `main`; two S-session near-misses started by editing it.
- Re-install no-mistakes (above) and re-warm the build in the background while doing doc work.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/perf/common.sh — shared helpers for the P1-PERF load/stress harness.
#
# Sourced by every s*-*.sh scenario and by run-all.sh. Nothing here measures
# anything on its own; it supplies the four things every scenario needs:
#
#   * a scenario workspace   — fresh data dir + a seeded git repo (demo.sh's
#                              recipe: .sergeant/workflows/<name>/<stage>/)
#   * a daemon under control — spawned with a chosen SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT, its pid
#                              read from the runtime descriptor (the documented
#                              client handshake), stopped and verified stopped
#   * /proc sampling         — VmRSS / VmHWM / threads / fd count / utime+stime
#                              into CSV, either one row on demand or a
#                              background sampler at a chosen interval
#   * measurement plumbing   — latency timing, percentiles, a summary block
#                              that is printed and written as JSON, and the
#                              hygiene sweep
#
# The harness drives the shipped release binary and its loopback HTTP API and
# adds no Rust (P1-PERF non-goal: "new Rust code beyond what a scenario
# strictly needs"). High-rate cells drive POST /v1/... with curl rather than
# one CLI process per call, because the CLI spawns a process per call and that
# is the client's cost, not the daemon's.
#
# Nothing under here writes into the repository tree: every scenario's data
# dirs, repos and raw output live under the <outdir> it is given.

# --- resolution ------------------------------------------------------------

PERF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PERF_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$PERF_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# The unit under test is the release build (P1-PERF: "the baseline describes
# what ships, not debug-profile DuckDB").
SGT_BIN="${SGT_BIN:-$PERF_REPO_ROOT/target/release/sgt}"

PERF_CLK_TCK="$(getconf CLK_TCK 2>/dev/null || echo 100)"

# Timing: CLOCK_REALTIME nanoseconds. `date +%s%N` costs a fork (~2 ms on this
# container) which is the same order as the thing being measured, so the
# fork-free bash-5 EPOCHREALTIME is preferred and `date` is the fallback. Same
# clock, same units.
perf_now_ns() {
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    printf '%s%s\n' "$sec" "${frac:0:9}"
  else
    date +%s%N
  fi
}

# perf_mark VAR — assign "now" in ns to VAR without forking a subshell.
perf_mark() {
  local -n __perf_mark_out=$1
  local t=${EPOCHREALTIME:-}
  if [ -n "$t" ]; then
    t=${t/,/.}
    local sec=${t%.*} frac=${t#*.}
    while [ ${#frac} -lt 9 ]; do frac="${frac}0"; done
    __perf_mark_out="${sec}${frac:0:9}"
  else
    __perf_mark_out="$(date +%s%N)"
  fi
}

perf_die() { printf '\033[31mperf: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
perf_say() { printf '   %s\n' "$*"; }
perf_step() { printf '\n\033[1m== %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
perf_warn() { printf '\033[33m   ! %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; }

perf_require_binary() {
  [ -x "$SGT_BIN" ] || perf_die "no release binary at $SGT_BIN (cargo build --release)"
  for tool in curl jq python3 git; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || perf_die "missing required tool: $tool"
  done

  # scenario tracks the checkout, not the binary: a commit landing mid-matrix

  if [ -z "${PERF_COMMIT:-}" ]; then

# --- scenario lifecycle ----------------------------------------------------

# perf_init <outdir> <scenario-name>
#

# P1-PERF harness

Load, stress and resource baseline for the shipped `sgt` release binary. Drives
the binary and its loopback HTTP API only — no new Rust, no test hooks.

```sh
cargo build --release                 # the unit under test
scripts/perf/run-all.sh /path/outdir  # environment + idle baseline + S1..S7, in order
scripts/perf/s3-deep.sh /path/outdir  # any scenario, alone
```

`<outdir>` must live **outside the repo tree**. Each scenario creates its own
data dir and seed repo under `<outdir>/scratch/`, writes raw CSV/JSON next to
it, prints a distilled summary block, and ends with the hygiene sweep.

| script | scenario |
| --- | --- |
| `idle-baseline.sh` | idle daemon, 2 min sampled (RSS, fds, CPU) |
| `s1-burst.sh` | concurrent submit bursts 1/5/10/20/50 |
| `s2-churn.sh` | 200 works in waves of 10 + leak watch |
| `s3-deep.sh` | one work driven to ≥1,000 events, then graph/show/events load |
| `s4-sse.sh` | 25 SSE subscribers through a burst; 10 killed mid-flight |
| `s5-journal.sh` | grow to 10k/25k/50k events; cold-start rebuild + analytics |
| `s6-crash.sh` | `kill -9` mid-burst ×3, restart, recovery assertions |
| `s7-clients.sh` | TUI under tmux, dashboard, `web`/`doctor`/`status`, orphan SIGTERM |

`common.sh` holds the shared helpers (daemon control, `/proc` sampling, seed
repo, percentiles, hygiene sweep); `_submit-one.sh` and `_get-one.sh` are the
single-call workers `xargs -P` fans out.

## Knobs

Every scenario reads its scale from the environment and documents its own knobs
in its header — e.g. `PERF_S1_BURSTS`, `PERF_S2_TOTAL`, `PERF_S5_MARKS`. Set
them to shrink a run for a smoke test:

```sh
PERF_S1_BURSTS="1 2" PERF_S1_SETTLE=1 scripts/perf/s1-burst.sh /tmp/out/s1
PERF_ONLY="s4 s6" scripts/perf/run-all.sh /tmp/out    # subset of the matrix
```

## What the fake script means

`SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT` is one **global FIFO of steps shared by the whole daemon**,
not a per-work program. One step is consumed per execution START and one per
input SEND; when it runs out, every later step is the default `complete`.
Measured on this build:

```
SGT_FAKE_SCRIPT="needs_input:q1;needs_input:q2;needs_input:q3;complete:a;needs_input:q4;complete:b"
submit    -> stage 1 START pops q1        -> needs_input
respond 1 -> SEND pops q2                 -> needs_input
respond 2 -> SEND pops q3                 -> needs_input
respond 3 -> SEND pops complete:a         -> stage 1 done, stage 2 START pops q4 -> needs_input
respond 4 -> SEND pops complete:b         -> work completed
```

Consequences for scenarios: a scripted multi-cycle flow is only deterministic
with **one work in flight** (S3 runs one work alone for exactly this reason),
and every scenario that wants "everything completes" simply leaves the variable
unset.

Event arithmetic on this build, for sizing a run: a completing two-stage work is
**16 journal events**; a scripted work is 10 events at submit plus **5 per
respond cycle** (so ≥1,000 events ≈ 200 cycles); journal bytes are ~550 per
event.

## Rules the harness obeys

- Measures, never fixes. A defect is a number plus a rerun, not a patch.
- Nothing is written into the repo tree except this directory.
- `perf_hygiene` separates *populated* surface dirs (a worktree that outlived
  its work) from *empty* leftovers, and a worktree held by a non-terminal work
  is expected residue, not a leak — read `hygiene-<label>.txt` before calling
  a sweep dirty.
- A daemon that needs SIGKILL to stop is recorded (`daemon_force_killed`), not
  quietly cleaned up.

Found during the Cerberus baseline run (docs/perf/baseline-cerberus-2026-08-11.md, Anomalies): each scenario summary records `commit` via `git rev-parse` at scenario start. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# P1-PERF — the whole matrix, in order, one command.
     3	#
     4	#   scripts/perf/run-all.sh <outdir>
     5	#
     6	# Records the environment, takes the idle-daemon baseline, then runs S1..S7
     7	# strictly sequentially — never overlapping another scenario's measurement
     8	# window, each into its own subdirectory of <outdir>, each against its own
     9	# fresh data dir. A scenario that fails is recorded as failed and the run
    10	# continues: "a scenario that cannot hit its target records where it stopped
    11	# and why — that is data, not failure."
    12	#
    13	# Every scenario is also runnable alone: scripts/perf/s3-deep.sh <outdir>.
    14	#
    15	# Knobs: PERF_ONLY ("s1 s4" to run a subset), PERF_SKIP_IDLE=1.
    16	# Scenario-level knobs are documented in each scenario's header and pass
    17	# through this script unchanged.
    18	set -uo pipefail
    19	
    20	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    21	# shellcheck source=common.sh
    22	. "$HERE/common.sh"
    23	
    24	OUT="${1:?usage: run-all.sh <outdir>}"
    25	mkdir -p "$OUT"
    26	OUT="$(cd "$OUT" && pwd)"
    27	perf_require_binary
    28	
    29	LOG="$OUT/run-all.log"
    30	STATUS="$OUT/run-all-status.tsv"
    31	: > "$STATUS"
    32	
    33	{
    34	  echo "P1-PERF full run"
    35	  echo "started: $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    36	  echo "outdir:  $OUT"
    37	  echo
    38	  PERF_OUT="$OUT" perf_environment "$OUT/environment.txt"
    39	} | tee "$LOG"
    40	
    41	ONLY="${PERF_ONLY:-}"
    42	wanted() {
    43	  [ -z "$ONLY" ] && return 0
    44	  case " $ONLY " in *" $1 "*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
    45	}
    46	
    47	run_stage() { # run_stage <name> <script> <subdir>
    48	  local name="$1" script="$2" sub="$3"
    49	  wanted "$name" || { printf '%s\tskipped\t0\n' "$name" >> "$STATUS"; return 0; }
    50	  printf '\n\033[1m######## %s ########\033[0m\n' "$name" | tee -a "$LOG"
    51	  local t0 t1 rc
    52	  perf_mark t0
    53	  "$script" "$OUT/$sub" 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG"
    54	  rc="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
    55	  perf_mark t1
    56	  printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$name" "$([ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && echo ok || echo "failed(rc=$rc)")" "$(perf_s $((t1 - t0)))" >> "$STATUS"
    57	  # Between scenarios: nothing of this one may still be running.
    58	  sleep 3
    59	}
    60	
    61	if [ "${PERF_SKIP_IDLE:-0}" != 1 ]; then
    62	  run_stage idle "$HERE/idle-baseline.sh" idle
    63	fi
    64	run_stage s1 "$HERE/s1-burst.sh"   s1
    65	run_stage s2 "$HERE/s2-churn.sh"   s2
    66	run_stage s3 "$HERE/s3-deep.sh"    s3
    67	run_stage s4 "$HERE/s4-sse.sh"     s4
    68	run_stage s5 "$HERE/s5-journal.sh" s5
    69	run_stage s6 "$HERE/s6-crash.sh"   s6
    70	run_stage s7 "$HERE/s7-clients.sh" s7
    71	
    72	printf '\n\033[1m######## run complete ########\033[0m\n' | tee -a "$LOG"
    73	{
    74	  printf '%-8s %-16s %s\n' scenario outcome wall_s
    75	  while IFS=$'\t' read -r name outcome wall; do
    76	    printf '%-8s %-16s %s\n' "$name" "$outcome" "$wall"
    77	  done < "$STATUS"
    78	} | tee -a "$LOG"
    79	
    80	# Final sweep across everything the run created.
    81	PERF_OUT="$OUT" PERF_SCENARIO=run-all PERF_SUMMARY_TSV="$OUT/run-all-summary.tsv" PERF_REPOS=()
    82	: > "$OUT/run-all-summary.tsv"
    83	for repo in "$OUT"/*/scratch/*/repo; do [ -d "$repo" ] && PERF_REPOS+=("$repo"); done
    84	perf_hygiene final | tee -a "$LOG"
    85	
    86	python3 - "$OUT" <<'PY' | tee -a "$LOG"
    87	# One index of every distilled summary the run produced, so the baseline doc
    88	# has a single place to read the matrix out of.
    89	import glob, json, os, sys
    90	out = sys.argv[1]

content.text:
**No candidates.**

I read the diff and traced every caller. On the efficiency axis the change is strictly fork-negative, and I could not construct a scenario where it adds work:

- `scripts/perf/common.sh:83-86` — the `rev-parse` is guarded and the result is `export`ed, so each scenario process spawned by `run-all.sh` inherits the value and skips the fork entirely. Per full matrix run the fork count goes from ~2 per process × 9 processes (idle + s1..s7 + run-all) down to 1 for the whole run.
- `scripts/perf/common.sh:115` and `scripts/perf/common.sh:689` are pure removals of a `git` fork (~2ms each per the file header's own accounting), and both sat on scenario-startup paths, not measurement loops.
- `perf_require_binary` is only called from `scripts/perf/common.sh:99` (inside `perf_init`, once per scenario) and `scripts/perf/run-all.sh:27` — never from a loop, and never from the per-call fan-out helpers `scripts/perf/_submit-one.sh` / `scripts/perf/_get-one.sh`, which do not source `common.sh` at all. So no fork was pushed into a hot path.
- The only theoretical new cost is `run-all.sh:27` now forking `git` in a call site that previously did zero git work, but that same process immediately calls `perf_environment` at `scripts/perf/run-all.sh:38`, which used to do exactly that fork — net zero for that process, net negative for its children. Not worth a finding.
- The extra exported variable adds ~50 bytes to the environment of every `curl`/daemon exec in high-rate cells; that is below measurement noise and not a nameable cost.

One non-efficiency observation, offered only because it's adjacent and cheap to state: the guard caches a failed `rev-parse` as the literal string `unknown` for the remainder of the run (`scripts/perf/common.sh:84`), so a transient git failure at `perf_require_binary` time permanently pins every scenario's `commit` field — the opposite of the staleness bug the comment cites. That's a correctness/robustness matter for another reviewer's axis, not wasted work.

Findings from a line-by-line scan of the changed hunks (all paths repo-relative to the repo root above).

**1. `scripts/perf/common.sh:83` — the `-z` guard trusts any pre-existing `PERF_COMMIT` from the ambient environment, with no validation and no warning.**
The whole point of the change is that the recorded commit must describe the binary, but the guard makes an inherited value authoritative over the actual repo. Failure scenario: a CI job (or a dev's `~/.bashrc`, or a wrapper that already exports a `PERF_COMMIT` for its own purposes — the name is generic) has `PERF_COMMIT=<PR head sha>` in the environment while the runner has checked out and built a merge commit. `./scripts/perf/run-all.sh /tmp/out` -> `environment.txt` and all 8 `*-summary.json` files stamp the PR head sha; the binary was built from the merge commit. Same shape as issue #50, only now it is uniform and therefore harder to spot. Nothing ever re-derives or cross-checks (e.g. against `sgt --version`), and there is no `perf_warn` when the value is inherited rather than computed.

**2. `scripts/perf/common.sh:85` — `export PERF_COMMIT` lives inside the `if`, so a set-but-unexported `PERF_COMMIT` is never exported and the pin does not propagate.**
Failure scenario: any caller that sets the variable without exporting it — e.g. an operator pinning a rerun with `PERF_COMMIT=abc123 bash -c './scripts/perf/run-all.sh /tmp/out'` where the assignment lands as a shell variable of the wrapper, or a future edit to `run-all.sh` that does `PERF_COMMIT="$(...)"` before line 27. `run-all.sh`'s own output uses the value (it is in scope), but `run_stage` spawns `s1..s7` as child processes (line 53), which do **not** inherit it; each child's `perf_require_binary` re-reads live `HEAD`. Result: `environment.txt` says one commit, the per-scenario summaries say another, and scenarios straddling a mid-matrix `git pull` disagree with each other — exactly the bug being fixed. `export PERF_COMMIT` belongs outside the `if`.

**3. `scripts/perf/common.sh:84` — a one-shot `|| echo unknown` now poisons the whole matrix instead of one scenario, and the failure is silenced.**
Failure scenario: the repo is owned by a different uid than the runner (common in containers/CI), so `git rev-parse HEAD` fails with the "dubious ownership / safe.directory" error; `2>/dev/null` swallows the diagnostic. `PERF_COMMIT` becomes the literal `unknown`, is exported, and because `unknown` is non-empty every one of the 7 child scenarios skips its own rev-parse and inherits it. Previously each scenario retried independently, so a transient failure (e.g. `index.lock` contention from a concurrent git operation, or an in-progress rebase/bisect leaving HEAD momentarily unreadable at harness start) cost at most one field; now a single unlucky moment at `perf_require_binary` time makes the entire run's commit field `unknown` with no way to tell it apart from a genuine non-repo run.

**4. `scripts/perf/common.sh:115` — an inherited `PERF_COMMIT` flows unvalidated into the TSV that `perf_summary`'s Python parser splits on tabs/newlines.**
`perf_kv` (line 131) is `printf '%s\t%s\n'` and the parser at lines 139-145 does `key, _, value = line.partition("\t")` per line. A rev-parse result could never contain whitespace; an environment variable can. Failure scenario: `PERF_COMMIT=$'abc123\n(dirty)'` (a wrapper that appends a dirtiness marker) -> `perf_kv` emits two lines, and the second is parsed as a *key* `(dirty)` with an empty value, so `<scenario>-summary.json` gains a bogus top-level key and the printed summary table gains a phantom row. A tab in the value likewise smuggles a second field. Worth at least constraining the inherited value (e.g. `[[ $PERF_COMMIT =~ ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$ ]]`) before trusting it.

**5. `scripts/perf/common.sh:689` vs `:115` — the two readers disagree on strictness, so a missing pin is a hard abort in one place and a silent `unknown` in the other.**
`perf_environment` uses `${PERF_COMMIT:-unknown}` while `perf_init` uses a bare `$PERF_COMMIT`. Every scenario runs `set -euo pipefail`, so any path reaching `perf_init`'s line 115 without `perf_require_binary` having run in the *same* shell dies with `PERF_COMMIT: unbound variable` — where the old code degraded to `unknown`. Conversely, `run-all.sh:38` calls `perf_environment` inside a `{ ... } | tee "$LOG"` **subshell**, so it only works because of the now-load-bearing `perf_require_binary` at `run-all.sh:27`, which reads as redundant (perf_init calls it too). Failure scenario: someone deletes that line 27 as dead code -> `environment.txt` silently records `commit: unknown` for the whole run, and moving the `perf_require_binary` call into the `{ }` block would not fix it, because the export would die with the subshell.

**6. `scripts/perf/common.sh:78-86` (comment + capture point) — the pin is tied to `HEAD` at harness start, not to the binary, so the stated failure mode is not actually eliminated.**
Failure scenario: the exact case in the comment — a commit lands mid-matrix. The operator pulls and runs `cargo build --release` while s4 is running; s5-s7 execute a genuinely different binary. With the change, all 8 scenarios now report the *pre-pull* commit, so 3 of 8 are wrong and, unlike before, the summaries are internally consistent and give no hint that the binary changed. The identity that is actually checkable is the binary's (`"$SGT_BIN" --version`, already captured in `perf_environment`, or its mtime/hash); a rev-parse at t=0 only narrows the window rather than closing it.

## Candidate findings (Simplification)

**1. `scripts/perf/common.sh:689` — the `:-unknown` default is unreachable, and contradicts the sibling consumer at line 115**
Both `perf_environment` call sites are already preceded by `perf_require_binary` (`scripts/perf/run-all.sh:27` directly; `scripts/perf/idle-baseline.sh:22` via `perf_init` → `perf_require_binary` at line 99), so `PERF_COMMIT` is always set here. `perf_init` states the real invariant (`"$PERF_COMMIT"`, bare); `perf_environment` denies it.
*failure_scenario:* Two readings of the same variable in one file assert opposite invariants, so the next maintainer cannot tell whether "unset" is a supported state. If they conclude it is, they add `:-unknown` at line 115 too; if they conclude it isn't, they still leave line 689 alone because removing it looks risky. Meanwhile a genuine ordering regression (someone calling `perf_environment` before `perf_require_binary`) fails loudly at line 115 under `set -u` but silently writes `commit: unknown` into `environment.txt` at line 689 — the least-debuggable outcome for the exact field issue #50 is about. Note also this is the *third* "unknown" fallback in the chain (`rev-parse … || echo unknown` at line 84 already guarantees a non-empty value).

**2. `scripts/perf/common.sh:78-87` — commit capture is hidden in a requirements checker, making `run-all.sh:27` load-bearing without saying so**
`perf_require_binary`'s name and body (executable check + `command -v` loop) advertise pure validation; it now also seeds and exports cross-process state that the whole issue-#50 fix depends on.
*failure_scenario:* `run-all.sh:27` calls `perf_require_binary` and then every scenario it spawns calls it again via `perf_init` — so the line looks redundant and is an obvious deletion for anyone tidying `run-all.sh`. Deleting it (or moving `perf_environment` above it) makes each scenario capture its own HEAD again, silently reinstating the exact mid-matrix skew of issue #50, with no test or assertion anywhere to catch it. Nothing in the function's name or the block's comment warns that the pin's correctness lives in that call ordering.

**3. `scripts/perf/common.sh:83-86` — four lines of guard-plus-export where the resolution section already has the right idiom**
`PERF_DIR`, `PERF_REPO_ROOT` and `SGT_BIN` (lines 30-34) are exactly this: process identity resolved once at source time, with `SGT_BIN` using `${SGT_BIN:-…}` for the override case. The same job is `: "${PERF_COMMIT:=$(git -C "$PERF_REPO_ROOT" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)}"; export PERF_COMMIT` placed beside line 34 — set for *every* consumer at source time, which dissolves finding 1 (no unset state to defend against) and finding 2 (no dependence on call order) at once, for one extra fork per sourced script.
*failure_scenario:* As written, harness identity is split across two locations with different conventions, so future identity fields (the binary mtime/hash issue #50 actually asks for) get scattered too — some at line 34, some inside `perf_require_binary` — and each new field re-litigates "is it set yet?" at every read site.

**4. `scripts/perf/common.sh:84` — the pin still derives from the checkout, not the binary, so the recorded value can still be wrong (now uniformly)**
Issue #50 (`ISSUE-50.md:10`) asks the field to "pin the binary's identity (e.g. hash the binary, or record rev-parse once at `perf_require_binary` time **alongside the binary mtime**)". Only the first half landed; nothing records `stat -c %Y "$SGT_BIN"` or a hash, and `perf_environment` (line 690) still prints only the binary's path.
*failure_scenario:* Run the matrix against a `target/release/sgt` built before the last few commits (the common case — the harness never rebuilds, it only checks `-x` at line 74). All 8 scenarios now agree on a commit whose code is not in the binary, and unlike the old per-scenario skew there is no disagreement between summaries to signal it — the baseline doc records a confidently wrong provenance with nothing left to cross-check it against, which is how the original anomaly was caught (binary mtime).

**5. `scripts/perf/common.sh:78-82` — five lines of incident narrative attached to a four-line block, none of which states what the guard is actually for**
The comment explains the *history* ("6 of 8 scenarios", issue #50) but not the mechanism: `-z` matters only because `run-all.sh` exports the value into children, i.e. the guard exists to *honor an inherited value*, not to "capture exactly once" (within a single process the capture is trivially once).
*failure_scenario:* A maintainer reading only the comment sees a within-process memoization and removes the `-z` guard as pointless in a function called once per process — which drops the inherited pin and restores per-scenario HEAD reads. The prose that would have prevented it is the one sentence the comment omits; the incident detail belongs in the commit message or `ISSUE-50.md`, which already holds it verbatim.

Read all relevant files plus the baseline doc that motivated the change (`docs/perf/baseline-cerberus-2026-08-11.md:105`, issue #50's actual writeup). Findings below.

**Verified clean:** every in-repo caller of `perf_environment` (`scripts/perf/run-all.sh:38`, `scripts/perf/idle-baseline.sh:22`) and every `perf_init` call (`idle-baseline.sh:17`, `s1..s7` lines 21-27) has `perf_require_binary` on its own path — `run-all.sh:27` runs before line 38, and `perf_init` calls it at `common.sh:99` before using `$PERF_COMMIT` at line 115. So question (1) has no in-tree violation. The problems are all in (2) and (3).

---

**1. `scripts/perf/common.sh:83` — exported pin leaks across logically separate runs from the same ancestor shell; the new binary is labelled with the old commit.**
`export PERF_COMMIT` plus a `[ -z ]` guard means the value is inherited, never refreshed. Failure scenario: an operator sources the library into an interactive shell (it is a `. `-sourced library; `run-all.sh:22` and every scenario do exactly this) and runs `perf_init`/`s1-burst.sh out1`. `PERF_COMMIT` is now exported in that shell. They then `git pull && cargo build --release` and run `scripts/perf/s3-deep.sh out2` from the *same* shell — the child inherits the stale sha and every summary JSON plus `environment.txt` for the new run reports the previous checkout's commit. The old code re-read HEAD per call and would have reported the new sha. Worse, the failure is undetectable by the exact method the baseline doc used to catch issue #50 (cross-scenario `commit` disagreement), because all scenarios now copy one variable.

**2. `scripts/perf/common.sh:84` — a transient git failure pins the literal string `unknown` for the entire matrix, with no retry.**
`|| echo unknown` assigns a non-empty value, so the `[ -z ]` guard never re-attempts. Failure scenario: `run-all.sh` is started in a container/CI where `git` rejects `PERF_REPO_ROOT` with "detected dubious ownership" (or an `index.lock` / mid-rebase state) at `run-all.sh:27`. `PERF_COMMIT=unknown` is exported; the operator notices and runs `git config --global --add safe.directory ...` two minutes in, but all 8 scenarios plus `environment.txt` still record `commit: unknown` for the whole ~7-minute run. Under the old code only the scenarios that started during the broken window were affected and later ones self-healed. The exported `unknown` also survives into any further scripts launched from that same shell (compounds with finding 1).

**3. `scripts/perf/common.sh:83` — the guard silently trusts an externally-set `PERF_COMMIT` with zero validation.**
Nothing checks the inherited value is a sha, is 40 hex chars, or corresponds to `PERF_REPO_ROOT` at all. Failure scenario: a CI wrapper (or an unrelated tool) exports `PERF_COMMIT` set to the PR *merge* sha, a short sha, or a branch name; `perf_kv commit` (line 115) and `environment.txt` (line 689) record that verbatim as the identity of the tested binary, and a baseline doc is later written citing it as ground truth (`baseline-cerberus-2026-08-11.md:5` cites `s1-burst-summary.json`'s `commit` field exactly this way). Previously the field was always a real HEAD sha of the checkout under test and could not be spoofed by the ambient environment.

**4. `scripts/perf/common.sh:78-82` (comment) vs `:84` (code) — the pin still reads the *checkout*, not the binary, so issue #50 is only half-fixed while its detection signal is removed.**
The comment claims to capture "the tested binary's identity", but the value is still `git rev-parse HEAD` — just once, earlier. Failure scenario: a concurrent session lands commits at 06:02 and the operator starts `run-all.sh` at 06:05 without rebuilding (`target/release/sgt` still from `f9b047d`). All 8 scenarios now uniformly report `5d3b333`, i.e. code that was never in the binary, and they *agree*, so the "commit drifts across scenarios" anomaly that let the human reconstruct the truth in `baseline-cerberus-2026-08-11.md:105` no longer fires. The mtime cross-check mentioned there is manual and outside the harness; nothing in the harness compares `SGT_BIN`'s mtime or `--version` against the pinned sha.

**5. `scripts/perf/common.sh:689` — the `unknown` fallback makes `perf_environment` silently degrade for any caller that has not run `perf_require_binary`.**
`perf_environment` is a public helper of a sourced library and is the only function that produces `environment.txt`, the artifact baseline docs quote. Failure scenario: someone regenerates an environment record ad hoc — `bash -c '. scripts/perf/common.sh; perf_environment /tmp/env.txt'` — or a future script calls `perf_environment` before `perf_require_binary` (nothing enforces ordering; `run-all.sh` only happens to call it at line 27). The file is written with `commit: unknown` and no warning, whereas the removed code always produced a real sha in exactly that context. There is no `perf_warn` on the fallback path.

**6. `scripts/perf/common.sh:115` vs `:689` — inconsistent unset-handling between the two replaced sites.**
`perf_kv commit "$PERF_COMMIT"` is unguarded while `perf_environment` uses `${PERF_COMMIT:-unknown}`. Failure scenario: scenarios run under `set -euo pipefail` (`idle-baseline.sh:10`, all `s*.sh`); any future refactor that reaches `perf_init` without `perf_require_binary` having set the variable — e.g. splitting the tool-check out of `perf_require_binary`, or a caller that does `unset PERF_COMMIT` after init and re-enters `perf_init` for a second scenario in-process — aborts the whole scenario with `PERF_COMMIT: unbound variable` at line 115 instead of recording `unknown` like its sibling. The old code could not fail this way because the value was computed inline at both sites.

## Verdict: not "no candidates" — the pin is a half-implementation of the issue's own prescription

Key facts established:

- **No build.rs anywhere in the repo** (`find . -name build.rs` outside `target/` returns nothing), no `vergen` in Cargo.toml, and no `GIT_HASH`/`GIT_COMMIT` env embedding in `src/`. The only version data in the binary is `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`.
- `src/cli.rs:38-41` uses clap's bare `version`, so `sgt --version` prints `sgt 0.1.0` — a hand-maintained constant unchanged since the crate was created. It carries **zero** build identity.
- `run-all.sh` never builds. `scripts/perf/README.md:7` lists `cargo build --release` as an operator prerequisite. The harness has no relationship to the build event at all.
- ISSUE-50.md asks for: *"record rev-parse once at `perf_require_binary` time **alongside the binary mtime**"*. The fix implements clause one and drops clause two — and mtime is precisely what the analyst used to recover ground truth (`docs/perf/baseline-cerberus-2026-08-11.md:105`).

### Candidate findings

**1. `scripts/perf/common.sh:84` — pin resolves the checkout, not the build; stale-binary case is issue #50 with earlier timing**
`failure_scenario`: Operator builds at `f9b047d`, pulls/rebases 12 commits, then runs `run-all.sh` without rebuilding (the build is an out-of-harness README step, `run-all.sh:27` only checks `-x`). All 8 scenarios now report the newest HEAD. That is verbatim #50's complaint — "self-report commits whose code was never in the tested binary" — with the divergence moved from mid-matrix to pre-matrix. The fix closes the 7-minute window and leaves the unbounded one open.

**2. `scripts/perf/common.sh:84` — the pin removes the only signal that detected #50 in the first place**
`failure_scenario`: #50 was caught because the field *disagreed with itself* across scenarios (`f9b047d`/`5d3b333`/`81d83ba` in baseline doc line 105); that drift is what prompted the mtime forensics. After the pin, a wrong commit is uniformly wrong across all 8 summary JSONs and `environment.txt`, and reads as authoritative agreement. The harness trades a loud, self-diagnosing wrongness for a silent one — strictly worse for the next reader unless mtime corroboration is added.

**3. `scripts/perf/common.sh:78-86` — binary mtime, the issue's explicit second clause and the actual ground truth, is still recorded nowhere**
`failure_scenario`: No file under `scripts/perf/` stats `$SGT_BIN` (`grep` for `mtime|stat -c` hits only DuckDB sizes at `common.sh:590`, `s3-deep.sh:138`, `s5-journal.sh:97`). A future run that misreports has no in-artifact evidence to recover from — the next analyst must re-derive it by hand from a host that may have been rebuilt since. The deeper mechanism is ~3 lines at the same call site: record `stat -c %Y "$SGT_BIN"`, compare against `git log -1 --format=%ct HEAD`, and `perf_warn` when the binary predates HEAD's commit time (i.e. "binary is older than the checkout — rebuild or expect a wrong commit field"). That converts the manual forensics of baseline line 105 into an automatic guard, adds no Rust, and satisfies the issue as written.

**4. `src/cli.rs:38-41` + `scripts/perf/common.sh:691` — `sgt --version` is a constant, so its use as corroboration is illusory**
`failure_scenario`: `perf_environment` records `sgt --version:` and the baseline doc (line 5) cites it as confirming the commit — "matches `environment.txt` and `sgt --version`". Since the string is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` = `0.1.0` for every build ever produced, it can never disagree with anything; the corroboration is vacuous and will keep being cited as if it were evidence. The genuinely deep fix is making the binary self-identifying (build.rs or `vergen` emitting the git hash into the version string), after which the harness's git call becomes unnecessary rather than merely better-timed. Caveat worth surfacing to the author: P1-PERF's stated non-goal is "new Rust code beyond what a scenario strictly needs," so this is a project-level decision, not a drive-by — but it is the correct altitude, and finding 3 is the cheap approximation of it.

**5. `scripts/perf/common.sh:84` — `rev-parse HEAD` is blind to a dirty working tree**
`failure_scenario`: Perf runs during development build from an uncommitted tree (this repo's current state is exactly that — `scripts/perf/common.sh` itself is modified and uncommitted). The summary stamps a clean hash whose code is not what was compiled, and unlike #50 there is no drift to expose it. `git describe --always --dirty` or appending a `git status --porcelain` flag is a one-token upgrade at the same line.

**6. `scripts/perf/common.sh:83` — the `[ -z "${PERF_COMMIT:-}" ]` guard makes an inherited value authoritative and rebuild-proof**
`failure_scenario`: Two matrices from one interactive shell that has sourced `common.sh` (or a CI runner exporting `PERF_COMMIT` for unrelated reasons): the second run is stamped with the first run's hash even after an intervening rebuild, and the value is never validated as a real commit. Minor, but it is a new failure mode the per-scenario `rev-parse` did not have; scoping the pin to "unset unless exported by run-all.sh in this invocation," or re-verifying with `git cat-file -e`, keeps the inheritance benefit without it.

## Verdict

The binary does **not** embed a build commit — so the diff is not duplicating a binary-side mechanism, but it also isn't the fix issue #50 asked for, and there *is* an existing in-repo idiom for artifact identity it bypasses.

Confirmed negatives (searched exhaustively): no `build.rs` anywhere in the crate, `vergen` appears 0 times in `Cargo.lock`, and `grep` for `git_hash|GIT_HASH|GIT_SHA|build_commit` over `src/` returns nothing. `sgt --version` is clap's derived `version` at `src/cli.rs:40`, which expands to `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` — i.e. the literal `0.1.0` in `Cargo.toml:3`. Same for the three other version sites (`src/api.rs:849`, `src/daemon.rs:290`, `src/telemetry.rs:686`): all `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, all static. So "read the identity from the binary itself" is not available today.

## Candidates

**1. `scripts/perf/common.sh:691` — `perf_environment` already records `sgt --version` as an identity field, and it carries zero commit information**
failure_scenario: The environment record now holds three identity fields (`commit:`, `binary:`, `sgt --version:`) that all fail to identify the build. `sgt --version` prints `sgt 0.1.0` on every commit for the whole MVP, so it is a duplicate identity slot that will never disambiguate two runs. The diff adds a fourth derivation (checkout HEAD) beside it instead of making one of the existing three actually binding.

**2. `scripts/coverage/c4-report.sh:67` — the sibling harness already has the artifact-identity idiom (`sha256sum` of the artifact), documented as policy in `scripts/coverage/README.md:39` and `:51`**
failure_scenario: `lcov_sha256` establishes the house pattern: when an artifact's identity matters, hash the artifact. The perf diff re-implements provenance from checkout state rather than reusing that one-line idiom on `$SGT_BIN`. Cost: two different provenance philosophies in two sibling harnesses under `scripts/`, and the perf one is the weaker of the two — a content hash is reproducible and survives a stale build, a HEAD read does neither.

**3. `scripts/perf/common.sh:84` — the pin still reads the checkout, so a stale `target/release/sgt` reproduces issue #50 exactly, minus the drift**
failure_scenario: `perf_require_binary` (line 76) only checks `[ -x "$SGT_BIN" ]`; it never checks the binary is newer than HEAD. Run the matrix without rebuilding after pulling, and all 8 summaries now agree on a commit whose code is not in the binary — worse than the drifting-commit bug it fixes, because unanimity reads as trustworthy. Issue #50 named the remedy as "hash the binary, **or** record rev-parse once at `perf_require_binary` time **alongside the binary mtime**"; the diff takes half of option two and drops the mtime that was doing the disambiguating work.

**4. `docs/perf/baseline-cerberus-2026-08-11.md:5` — the mtime cross-check the diff omits is currently a manual human step, and stays manual**
failure_scenario: The baseline's "Unit under test" line establishes the real commit by hand-comparing `target/release/sgt`'s mtime (Aug 11 05:58) against `git log` timestamps.
